lessons.titleEn: take the heavy lifting off people's shoulders
lessons.titleZh: 替人分擔最吃力的部分

target.pattern: \b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken) the heavy lifting off (?:people[’\x27]s|our|their|his|her|my|your) shoulders\b|\b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken) the heavy lifting out of\b

brief.meaningEn: Remove the most demanding part of a task from people, using a combined work-and-burden image.
brief.meaningZh: 用吃力工作及肩上負擔的意象，描述替人移除任務中最費力的部分。
brief.grammar: take the heavy lifting off someone’s shoulders OR take the heavy lifting out of + task; took/taken. The first names relieved people, while the second names the task made easier. Identify which work is removed and which responsibilities remain.
brief.register: A colleague describing a tool or helper to teammates can use this neutral work-and-burden metaphor. The two constructions share the same practical relief; neither promises an entirely automatic task.
brief.boundaryZh: 最吃力的部分減少，不等於整項工作已不用人參與；要交代實際移走的任務及仍需有人作的判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有人分擔與工作變得毫不費力不同，也不能由一句可能性的描述就宣稱已完成替代。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體說明哪部分負擔減輕，同時保留人仍要承擔的責任。

sources.sentence: The new system will take the heavy lifting out of routine checks.

listening.en: The new booking tool took the heavy lifting off our shoulders by matching the available rooms with the group sizes. We still checked access needs and confirmed the final choices with the organisers.
listening.zh: 新預訂工具按小組人數配對可用房間，替我們分擔最費力的部分。我們仍核對無障礙需要，並與統籌人確認最後選擇。
listening.promptZh: 工具減輕了甚麼？哪些工作仍由人處理？

options.en: It matched rooms and group sizes, while people still checked access and confirmed the choices.
options.zh: 它配對房間與小組人數，人仍須核對無障礙需要及確認選擇。

options.en: It confirmed every group’s access needs before the organisers supplied them.
options.zh: 統籌人還未提供資料，它已確認每組的無障礙需要。

options.en: The staff matched the rooms manually and used the tool only to print the final list.
options.zh: 職員自行配對房間，工具只用來列印最後名單。

options.en: The tool matched rooms by access requirements rather than by group size.
options.zh: 工具按無障礙需要配對房間，而不是按小組人數。

listening.explanationZh: 工具負責配對這個吃力部分；後句明確保留核對需要及最後確認的人工工作。

reply.promptEn: What useful difference did the booking tool make?
reply.promptZh: 預訂工具帶來甚麼實際幫助？

options.en: It took the heavy lifting off our shoulders by doing the initial room matching.
options.zh: 它處理初步房間配對，替我們分擔最費力的部分。

options.en: We no longer had to compare every room size with every group ourselves.
options.zh: 我們不用再親自把每個房間大小與每組人數逐一比較。

options.en: It handled a demanding comparison while leaving the final checks with us.
options.zh: 它處理費力的比較，最後核對仍由我們負責。

options.en: The matching work was reduced, so we could focus on needs the tool did not confirm.
options.zh: 配對工作減少，讓我們能專注工具沒有確認的需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都具體指出配對工作的減輕，沒有把它誇成全部責任已移走。

scene.promptZh: 整理活動報名時，助手只把你已核對好的名單換了字體；最費時的資格核對仍全由你做。有人說這已替你分擔最吃力的部分。哪句較準確？

options.en: Changing the font helped the presentation, but it did not take the heavy lifting off my shoulders if I still did the demanding checks.
options.zh: 換字體有助呈現，但如果費力的核對仍由我做，就不能說已替我分擔最吃力的部分。

options.en: The helper’s formatting shows that the eligibility checks were transferred to them.
options.zh: 助手調整格式，顯示資格核對已轉交給他。

options.en: The account says the main difficulty was choosing a readable font rather than checking eligibility.
options.zh: 敘述說，主要難處是選易讀字體，而不是核對資格。

scene.explanationZh: 需要看最吃力的工作是否真的移交，不能把任何小改善都說成已減輕主要負擔。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「The system may take the heavy lifting off our shoulders」推論？

options.en: 系統可能替我們處理一項費力工作。
系統已接手整項任務，人工判斷不再需要。
仍應確認哪些工作會減少，哪些需要保留。

contrast.explanationZh: may保留可能性；移走吃力部分也不等於接手全部任務。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「配對工具幫了忙，明天就不用問統籌人確認了吧？」你知道工具沒有記錄無障礙需要。哪句最好？

options.en: It took the heavy lifting off our shoulders, but we still need the organisers to confirm needs the tool does not record.
options.zh: 它替我們分擔最費力的部分，但工具沒有記錄的需要，仍須由統籌人確認。

options.en: I assumed a room that fits the group size must also meet the group’s access needs.
options.zh: 我以為房間容得下小組人數，就一定符合無障礙需要。

options.en: I thought confirmation had moved to the tool as soon as it began matching rooms.
options.zh: 我以為工具一開始配對房間，最後確認也已轉由它負責。

dialogue.explanationZh: 配對容量與確認無障礙需要不同；減輕一部分負擔，不會自動移交其他判斷。

speaking.en: The shared checklist can take the heavy lifting off our shoulders, but someone still needs to decide what each item requires.
speaking.zh: 共用核對表可以替我們分擔最費力的部分，但每項需要甚麼，仍要有人判斷。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清減少的工作及仍需人作的判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你正向地方歷史小組示範自動逐字稿。它可以先打出錄音內容，但遇到地方人名經常聽錯，發言者也未同意公開。用一至兩句英文提出先試一小段，再由熟悉人名的人覆核及詢問公開意願的方案；不宣布逐字稿已可直接發表。

examples.en: Automatic transcription could take the heavy lifting off our shoulders, but local names and permission to publish still need attention. Could we test a short passage, ask someone familiar with the names to check it, and confirm what the speakers want shared?
examples.zh: 自動逐字稿可能替我們分擔最費力的部分，但地方人名及公開許可仍須處理。我們可否先試一小段，請熟悉人名的人核對，再確認發言者願意分享甚麼？

examples.en: Let us see whether a short transcription trial can take the heavy lifting off our shoulders before we plan a full release. We should have the names checked by a local reader and ask the speakers about publication rather than treat a draft as ready to share.
examples.zh: 全面發布前，我們先用一小段逐字稿試驗，看看能否分擔最費力的部分。我們應請熟悉地方的人核對名字，並詢問發言者的公開意願，不把草稿當成已可分享。

glossary.en: treat a draft as ready to share

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出小範圍試驗及人名覆核、公開意願兩項後續安排；不要把打字工作減輕等同全部內容已正確或已獲同意。

takeaways.en: A volunteer took the heavy lifting off my shoulders by sorting the applications before I read the individual statements.
takeaways.zh: 一位義工先整理申請，讓我再讀個別陳述，替我分擔了最費力的部分。

takeaways.en: A simple booking form takes the heavy lifting out of collecting requests, but a coordinator still resolves clashes.
takeaways.zh: 簡單的預約表格減輕收集申請時最吃力的部分，但時段衝突仍由統籌人處理。

brief.meaningEn: Extremely hard and exhausting work, especially work requiring sustained physical effort.
brief.meaningZh: 形容工作非常吃力、令人疲憊，尤其是需要持續體力的工作。
brief.grammar: back-breaking work/labour; a backbreaking task. Both spellings occur. The adjective describes demanding effort, not a medical finding that a person’s back has broken.
brief.register: An established emphatic adjective built from a bodily image, rather than a multiword idiom. Use the context to explain the effort; do not infer an injury or a diagnosis.
brief.boundaryZh: 形容吃力不等於有人受傷，也不等於工作沒有價值；要看實際付出的體力及時間。
brief.misconceptionZh: 耗時、煩悶及體力吃重不是完全相同的描述；單憑工時長，未必知道身體負擔。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體動作說明吃力程度，並在描述工作時避免把修辭當成傷勢報告。

sources.sentence: Carrying sacks all day is back-breaking work.

listening.en: Moving the archive was back-breaking work: we carried heavy boxes up three flights of stairs for most of the morning. By lunchtime we were exhausted, although nobody reported an injury.
listening.zh: 搬遷檔案非常吃力：整個上午大部分時間，我們提着重箱走上三層樓梯。午飯時大家已筋疲力盡，但沒有人報告受傷。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼支持這個吃力的描述？

options.en: Repeatedly carrying heavy boxes upstairs left the group exhausted.
options.zh: 反覆把重箱搬上樓，讓大家筋疲力盡。

options.en: The group spent the morning checking box numbers while seated.
options.zh: 大家整個上午坐着核對箱號。

options.en: The description reports a confirmed back injury caused by the move.
options.zh: 描述報告了搬遷造成、已確認的背部傷勢。

options.en: The move was delayed mainly because the archive’s address was unclear.
options.zh: 搬遷主要因檔案室地址不清楚而延誤。

listening.explanationZh: 重箱、樓梯及反覆搬運解釋了體力負擔；修辭不是已確認傷勢，題目也明說沒有人報告受傷。

reply.promptEn: Why did you describe the move as exhausting?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說搬遷令人筋疲力盡？

options.en: It was back-breaking work carrying heavy boxes up three flights for much of the morning.
options.zh: 上午大部分時間都要把重箱搬上三層樓，工作非常吃力。

options.en: The repeated lifting and stair climbing required sustained physical effort.
options.zh: 反覆提箱及上樓，需要持續付出體力。

options.en: We had been hauling the boxes upstairs long enough to be worn out by lunch.
options.zh: 我們長時間把箱子搬上樓，午飯時已十分疲累。

options.en: The weight and repeated journeys made it much more demanding than checking the labels.
options.zh: 箱子的重量和反覆往返，讓工作遠比核對標籤吃力。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋具體體力負擔，不把沒有受傷說成工作輕鬆。

scene.promptZh: 一位訪問者只知道職員整天坐着等電話，覺得時間過得慢；他沒有問工作動作或疲勞情況，就稱工作back-breaking。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The account establishes a long wait, but not enough about the effort to justify calling it back-breaking.
options.zh: 敘述說明等待很久，但未交代足夠付出情況，不能據此稱工作非常吃力。

options.en: Waiting for many hours establishes the same physical demands as carrying heavy loads.
options.zh: 等了很多小時，就能確定體力要求與搬重物相同。

options.en: The account describes repeated lifting rather than waiting for a call.
options.zh: 敘述描述反覆提重物，而不是等電話。

scene.explanationZh: 可以形容等待漫長或煩悶，但這些資料本身沒有交代非常吃力的工作負擔。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「It was back-breaking work」確定？

options.en: 說話者把工作形容為非常吃力。
有人已由醫生確診背部骨折。
可以追問哪些動作或工作量造成負擔。

contrast.explanationZh: 這是強調吃力程度的形容詞，不是醫學診斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「沒有人受傷，所以你不能說搬箱很吃力吧？」你們午飯時已筋疲力盡。哪句最好？

options.en: It was back-breaking work because of the weight and repeated stairs; I am describing the effort, not reporting an injury.
options.zh: 工作因重量及反覆上樓而非常吃力；我是在形容付出，不是報告傷勢。

options.en: I thought the absence of an injury meant the work required little physical effort.
options.zh: 我以為沒有人受傷，就表示工作不太需要體力。

options.en: I took the adjective to mean the main problem was boredom rather than exertion.
options.zh: 我以為這個形容詞表示主要問題是煩悶，而不是費力。

dialogue.explanationZh: 付出的體力與是否受傷不同；上下文描述的是負重及反覆上樓，不只是煩悶。

speaking.en: She called the clearing job back-breaking because every load had to be carried by hand along the narrow path.
speaking.zh: 她說清理工作非常吃力，因為每批物品都要人手沿狹窄小徑搬運。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清這個形容詞所指的實際工作。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編寫地方展覽的一段說明。訪問中，一位昔日工人說每天人手把濕泥磚從院子搬到窯邊，反覆走很多趟；資料沒有提傷勢。用一至兩句英文寫實際展板文字，以具體動作說明工作吃力，不添寫骨折或醫療結論。

examples.en: The worker remembered back-breaking days carrying wet bricks by hand from the yard to the kiln. The weight and repeated journeys explain the effort in this account; it does not record an injury.
examples.zh: 工人記得那些非常吃力的日子，要人手把濕泥磚從院子搬到窯邊。重量及反覆往返說明了這段記錄中的付出，記錄並沒有提及傷勢。

examples.en: Carrying wet bricks to the kiln was back-breaking work, according to the former worker. Each day involved repeated journeys from the yard with loads that had to be moved by hand.
examples.zh: 據昔日工人所說，把濕泥磚搬到窯邊是非常吃力的工作。每天都要人手負重，從院子反覆往返。

glossary.en: from the yard to the kiln

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫可直接展示的說明，把形容詞連到濕泥磚、人工搬運及反覆往返；不把修辭擴寫成資料沒有提供的傷勢。

takeaways.en: The workers described the harvest as back-breaking after hours of bending and carrying full baskets.
takeaways.zh: 工人彎身及搬滿籃作物多個小時後，形容收成工作非常吃力。

takeaways.en: Her diary records back-breaking work on the hillside, with supplies carried up a path too narrow for a cart.
takeaways.zh: 她的日記記下山坡上非常吃力的工作：小徑太窄，手推車進不去，只能把物資搬上去。

brief.meaningEn: Think and respond quickly when an unprepared-for situation requires an immediate reaction.
brief.meaningZh: 遇到未預先準備的情況時，迅速思考並作出即場回應。
brief.grammar: think on your feet; thinking/thought on my/her/their feet. The possessive follows the person doing the thinking. It does not require standing up and does not excuse making up facts.
brief.register: Established idiom about mental agility and improvisation, often in live conversation or changing situations. Preparation can help someone respond; the idiom concerns the immediate adaptation.
brief.boundaryZh: 即場反應不等於胡猜，也不保證每次決定都正確；可以先澄清問題，或坦承某項資料需要核實。
brief.misconceptionZh: 熟練背誦與應付未預期變化不同，坐着的人也可以迅速應變。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述真正的即場調整，並提出誠實而具體的回應。

listening.en: I had to think on my feet when a visitor asked about an object missing from my prepared tour. Still seated beside the display, I used the label to explain what was known and said I would check the uncertain date.
listening.zh: 訪客問到導覽稿沒有包括的物品時，我得即場應變。我仍坐在展品旁，利用標籤解釋已知資料，並說會核對未能確定的日期。
listening.promptZh: 哪些做法顯示即場應變？

options.en: The guide adapted to an unexpected question and distinguished known information from a date needing a check.
options.zh: 導賞員回應未預期的問題，也分清已知資料及仍須核對的日期。

options.en: The visitor asked a rehearsed question that the guide answered from a memorised script.
options.zh: 訪客問了排練過的問題，導賞員照背好的稿回答。

options.en: The guide stood up so that the prepared script could be read aloud.
options.zh: 導賞員站起來，照讀已準備好的稿。

options.en: The guide supplied an exact date without mentioning any uncertainty.
options.zh: 導賞員給出準確日期，沒有提及任何不確定之處。

listening.explanationZh: 未預期的問題需要即時調整；坐着並不妨礙應變，核對日期也比猜一個日期更忠實。

reply.promptEn: How did you handle the question that was not in the tour?
reply.promptZh: 你怎樣處理導覽稿沒有包括的問題？

options.en: I had to think on my feet, using the label and admitting that the date needed checking.
options.zh: 我得即場應變，利用標籤，也承認日期需要核對。

options.en: I adapted the answer to the visitor instead of pretending it was in the prepared script.
options.zh: 我按訪客的問題調整回答，沒有假裝稿裏已有答案。

options.en: I explained the available information and left the uncertain point for a check.
options.zh: 我解釋手邊資料，把不確定之處留待核對。

options.en: I answered from the label and said I would check the uncertain date rather than pretend I knew it.
options.zh: 我按標籤回答，並說會核對未確定的日期，沒有假裝知道。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各自說明即場處理的方式，不把承認未確定資料當成沒有應變。

scene.promptZh: 演講者把熟練的五分鐘講稿照原次序背完，沒有被問問題，也沒有遇到安排改動。評語只憑流利，說這證明他即場應變能力。哪句較準確？

options.en: A fluent prepared speech does not by itself show that he can think on his feet in an unexpected situation.
options.zh: 流利地講出已準備的演講，本身不足以顯示他遇到意外情況時能即場應變。

options.en: The account describes him changing the argument after an unexpected challenge.
options.zh: 敘述描述，他遇到未預期的質疑後改了論點。

options.en: The fluency establishes that the speech was composed in response to the audience on the spot.
options.zh: 流利程度證明，演講是他現場按觀眾反應即席構思的。

scene.explanationZh: 可以肯定準備及流利，但題目沒有提供未預期變化或即時調整的資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只因一個人說「I had to think on my feet」就推論？

options.en: 他當時需要迅速作出回應。
他必定站着，而且給出的每項資料都已核實。
可以再問甚麼變化令他需要應變。

contrast.explanationZh: feet在這裏是慣用表達的一部分，不指定姿勢，也不保證資料及結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你承認日期不知道，就不算反應快吧？」你想保留誠實，也回答訪客眼前的問題。哪句最好？

options.en: Thinking on my feet meant choosing what I could explain reliably and saying what I would check, not inventing a date.
options.zh: 即場應變是選擇能可靠解釋的資料，並說明會核對甚麼，不是編一個日期。

options.en: I thought a quick answer had to include a definite date, even when the label did not give one.
options.zh: 我以為迅速回答一定要有明確日期，即使標籤沒有提供。

options.en: I assumed checking one uncertain detail meant none of the label’s information could be used.
options.zh: 我以為有一項細節要核對，就表示整張標籤的資料都不能用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 迅速作出有用而誠實的選擇，也可以是應變；不需要把未確定資料變成肯定答案。

speaking.en: She thought on her feet when the audience changed, replacing the technical opening with an example they could follow.
speaking.zh: 觀眾換了一批時，她即場應變，把技術性的開場換成大家能理解的例子。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說清楚需要即場調整的變化。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你主持學生分享會，原定簡報畫面突然不能顯示。你手上仍有講者的印刷綱要，而且有人可以讀給全場聽。用一至兩句英文直接向大家交代你會即場改用綱要、先徵求講者同意，再繼續；不宣布設備已修好。

examples.en: We need to think on our feet while the screen is unavailable: could we use the printed outline, with the speaker’s agreement? If that suits you, I can ask a reader to take us through it so we can continue without the slides.
examples.zh: 畫面不能顯示時，我們需要即場應變：講者若同意，我們可否改用印刷綱要？如果你覺得合適，我可以請人帶大家讀過，讓分享在沒有投影片的情況下繼續。

examples.en: I will have to think on my feet and suggest a change rather than wait for the screen. Would the speaker be happy for someone to read the printed outline aloud before we continue the discussion?
examples.zh: 我得即場應變，提出改動，而不只等畫面恢復。講者是否願意先讓人讀出印刷綱要，再繼續討論？

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫給現場聽眾的實際應變安排，使用仍可用的綱要並先問講者同意；不把替代方案說成設備已修復或已得到批准。

takeaways.en: The receptionist thought on her feet and found a quiet room when the visitor could not hear in the busy hall.
takeaways.zh: 訪客在繁忙大堂聽不清時，接待員即場應變，找了一間安靜房間。

takeaways.en: I had to think on my feet when two guests arrived together and both needed the only available interpreter.
takeaways.zh: 兩位來賓同時到場，都需要唯一在場的傳譯員，我得即場應變。

lessons.titleZh: 像鐘錶般順暢準時地運作

brief.meaningEn: Operate smoothly and as planned, with precise or reliable coordination.
brief.meaningZh: 運作順暢、按計劃進行，環節配合準確可靠。
brief.grammar: run/runs/ran like clockwork; was running like clockwork. Like clockwork can also describe regular occurrence, but this run-pattern focuses on smooth operation. No article before clockwork.
brief.register: Established machine comparison, often appreciative. A successful run is evidence about that occasion, not a promise that the system cannot fail later.
brief.boundaryZh: 順暢與單純速度快不同；也不表示不需要人準備、協調或留意參與者的經驗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 只看幕後表格整齊，未必知道實際等候或交接情況；要看活動是否真的按安排運作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體環節支持順暢的描述，也能查問觀察範圍以外的實際情況。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The small clinic runs like clockwork.

listening.en: The community meal ran like clockwork because the kitchen team timed each batch and the servers knew which tables were ready. Food reached the guests as planned, with no long wait between the main course and dessert.
listening.zh: 社區聚餐運作得像鐘錶般順暢，因為廚房掌握每批時間，服務員也知道哪些桌已準備好。食物按計劃送到賓客面前，主菜與甜品之間沒有久候。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼讓這次活動被形容為運作順暢？

options.en: The teams coordinated the batches and tables, so the courses reached guests as planned.
options.zh: 各組配合批次及桌上進度，讓菜式按計劃送到賓客面前。

options.en: The cooks finished all the food before the servers had been told which tables were ready.
options.zh: 服務員還未知道哪些桌已準備好，廚師就已煮完全部食物。

options.en: Guests waited through a long gap because the dessert delivery had not been planned.
options.zh: 甜品送達未有安排，賓客因此等了很久。

options.en: The team judged the event only from the speed of cooking, without considering table service.
options.zh: 團隊只按煮食速度判斷活動，沒有考慮送餐服務。

listening.explanationZh: 時間與桌上進度有協調，實際送餐也符合安排，才支持整體順暢的描述。

reply.promptEn: Why did you say the meal service went smoothly?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說聚餐服務順暢？

options.en: It ran like clockwork because the kitchen batches and table service were coordinated.
options.zh: 廚房批次與送餐互相配合，所以運作像鐘錶般順暢。

options.en: Everyone knew which tables were ready when each batch was prepared.
options.zh: 每批食物準備好時，大家都知道哪些桌可以上菜。

options.en: The main course and dessert arrived without the long gap we wanted to avoid.
options.zh: 主菜及甜品之間沒有出現我們想避免的久候。

options.en: The timing plan was reflected in what the guests actually experienced.
options.zh: 時間安排在賓客的實際經驗中得到體現。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用實際配合及送餐結果解釋順暢，不只評論表格或單一速度。

scene.promptZh: 包裝組每小時封好很多箱，但標籤常貼錯，寄件組要逐箱拆開重核。有人只看封箱速度，說整個寄件流程runs like clockwork。哪句較準確？

options.en: Fast packing does not mean the whole process runs like clockwork when labelling errors repeatedly interrupt dispatch.
options.zh: 如果標籤錯誤反覆阻礙寄件，封箱快不表示整個流程運作順暢。

options.en: The high packing rate shows that dispatch can proceed without further checks.
options.zh: 封箱速度高，顯示寄件可以不用再核對便繼續。

options.en: The account says label checking was completed before the boxes were sealed.
options.zh: 敘述說，封箱前已完成標籤核對。

scene.explanationZh: 順暢涉及整個流程是否配合；一段快，但下一段反覆返工，不能只靠速度概括。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「Yesterday’s service ran like clockwork」推論？

options.en: 昨天的服務運作順暢。
下次換人或換場地後，流程也必定不會出錯。
可以再問哪些準備及協調促成昨天的結果。

contrast.explanationZh: 一句話描述昨天的情況，不保證不同條件下的下一次表現。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「既然昨天順暢，下次換一組新義工，也不用再交接吧？」你知道新義工還未看過分工。哪句最好？

options.en: It ran like clockwork yesterday, but the new volunteers still need to understand the handover that made that possible.
options.zh: 昨天運作順暢，但新義工仍需要了解讓它順利的交接安排。

options.en: I assumed yesterday’s timing was enough for newcomers to know their roles without an explanation.
options.zh: 我以為昨天的時間安排，已足以讓新成員不用解釋就知道角色。

options.en: I would repeat the old timings without checking whether the new team can prepare the batches in the same way.
options.zh: 我會照用舊時間，不問新團隊能否按同一方式準備批次。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以肯定昨天，也仍要把必要安排交接給新團隊；舊結果不能代替新成員的了解。

speaking.en: The rehearsal ran like clockwork once each person knew the cue for passing the microphone.
speaking.zh: 每人知道何時傳咪後，排練就像鐘錶般順暢地進行。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把順暢運作連到具體配合。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫學生展覽的回顧。台前活動準時，負責人因此稱全場運作順暢，但你還未了解側門的等候隊伍及無障礙入口。用一至兩句英文給回顧小組提出實際查問安排，先確認這兩部分的經驗，不否定已觀察到的準時節目，也不先宣布全場都順利。

examples.en: The stage programme ran like clockwork, but could we ask about the side-door queue and the access entrance before describing the whole exhibition that way? Let us include those visitors’ experiences in the review as well as the timetable.
examples.zh: 台前節目運作得像鐘錶般順暢，但形容整個展覽也一樣之前，我們可否先問側門隊伍及無障礙入口的情況？回顧除了時間表，也應包括那些訪客的經驗。

examples.en: Before we say the exhibition ran like clockwork, I suggest checking with the people who used the side door and access entrance. We can keep the evidence that the programme was on time while finding out whether the other arrangements worked too.
examples.zh: 說整個展覽運作得像鐘錶般順暢之前，我建議先問使用側門及無障礙入口的人。我們可以保留節目準時的證據，同時了解其他安排是否也順利。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出具體查問對象及範圍，讓回顧包括尚未了解的入口經驗；不把台前準時直接擴成全部流程順暢。

takeaways.en: The book delivery ran like clockwork after the library and school agreed where each trolley should arrive.
takeaways.zh: 圖書館與學校議定每架手推車的送達位置後，送書流程運作得像鐘錶般順暢。

takeaways.en: The team wanted the changeover to run like clockwork, so they practised the equipment handover together.
takeaways.zh: 團隊想讓轉場像鐘錶般順暢，所以一起練習器材交接。

brief.meaningEn: Appear or happen, often when not expected; a name, topic or issue can recur in this way.
brief.meaningZh: 出現或發生，往往帶有未預期的意思；名字、話題或問題也可以這樣反覆出現。
brief.grammar: crop up; crops/cropped/cropping up, with doubled p in the past and -ing form. Intransitive: a question crops up, not someone crops a question up. Crop up in conversation/in a search.
brief.register: Common informal phrasal verb. The subject need not be a problem or something unwelcome; often unexpected does not mean every occurrence is surprising or harmful.
brief.boundaryZh: 出現不等於已處理，也不指定必定有壞影響；情況可以一次發生，也可以反覆出現。
brief.misconceptionZh: 名字在談話出現，不等於那個人已親身到場；同樣，有問題冒出，不等於當時已有答案。
brief.outcomeZh: 能交代出現的是甚麼及在何處出現，並按已有資料安排跟進。

listening.en: The same photographer’s name cropped up in three letters we were cataloguing. We had not been searching for her, so we noted the references and planned to check whether they concerned the same person.
listening.zh: 我們整理的三封信都出現同一位攝影師的名字。我們本來沒有在找她，所以記下提及之處，打算核對是否指同一個人。
listening.promptZh: 名字的出現讓整理者怎樣處理？

options.en: They noted the unexpected references and planned an identity check.
options.zh: 他們記下未預期的提及，並打算核對身份。

options.en: They had selected the three letters because the photographer was already their research subject.
options.zh: 他們因早已研究這位攝影師，才挑選那三封信。

options.en: They confirmed from the repeated name alone that the letters concerned one person.
options.zh: 他們單憑名字重複，就確認三封信指同一個人。

options.en: The photographer visited the catalogue team to explain the letters.
options.zh: 攝影師親身到訪整理小組，解釋那些信。

listening.explanationZh: 名字在文件中出現，並不是本人到訪；小組還打算核對，沒有只靠同名就完成確認。

reply.promptEn: What drew your attention to the photographer?
reply.promptZh: 甚麼令你們留意那位攝影師？

options.en: Her name cropped up in three letters even though we had not been looking for her.
options.zh: 她的名字出現在三封信中，而我們本來沒有在找她。

options.en: We noticed repeated references while cataloguing letters for another purpose.
options.zh: 我們為別的目的整理信件時，留意到反覆的提及。

options.en: The same name appeared often enough for us to note a possible connection.
options.zh: 同一名字多次出現，讓我們記下可能有關聯。

options.en: The letters brought an unplanned lead to our attention.
options.zh: 那些信讓我們留意到一條未預先安排的線索。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出名字或線索的出現，不擅自完成身份確認。

scene.promptZh: 座談中，一位作者的名字幾次被提及，但那位作者沒有到場，話題也沒有涉及麻煩。學生以為cropped up必定指有問題的人突然出現。哪句最準確？

options.en: A name can crop up in conversation without the person arriving or a problem arising.
options.zh: 名字可以在談話中出現，而不表示本人到場或有麻煩發生。

options.en: The repeated mentions establish that the author joined the discussion in person.
options.zh: 反覆提及，證明作者親身加入討論。

options.en: The phrase shows that the speakers had identified a problem with the author’s work.
options.zh: 這個表達顯示，說話者已發現作者作品有問題。

scene.explanationZh: crop up可以說名字在談話中出現；是否有麻煩或本人到場，要由其他資料交代。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「A question cropped up during the meeting」確定？

options.en: 會議中出現了一個問題。
問題在會議結束前已得到答案。
可以再了解問題的內容及後續安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 出現與得到解答是不同步驟；crop up本身沒有交代處理結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「三封信都提到同一名字，就不用再核對是否同一個人吧？」你想保留線索及不確定性。哪句最好？

options.en: The name cropped up several times, but repeated spelling alone does not settle whether the references identify one person.
options.zh: 名字出現了幾次，但拼寫重複，本身不足以確定提及的是同一個人。

options.en: I assumed repeated spelling was enough to complete the identity check.
options.zh: 我以為拼寫重複，已足以完成身份核對。

options.en: I thought noting the references meant we had already compared the dates and biographical details.
options.zh: 我以為記下提及之處，就表示我們已比較日期及生平資料。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以記錄有用線索，但仍要按日期及人物資料核對，不能把記下提及當成核對完成。

speaking.en: If another question crops up while you read the notes, write it beside the relevant passage so we can return to it.
speaking.zh: 讀筆記時若再出現問題，就把它寫在相關段落旁，方便我們回頭處理。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再交代出現問題後的具體跟進方法。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你主持讀書小組，討論中冒出一個關於譯本版本的問題，現場沒有可核實的資料。大家仍有另一段已準備好的討論。用一至兩句英文實際提議記下問題及所需資料，下一次帶版本頁回來核對，再繼續今天的段落；不猜答案或取消全場。

examples.en: A question about the edition has cropped up, and we do not have the details here to check it. Let us note what we need, bring the edition pages next time, and continue with the passage we prepared today.
examples.zh: 出現了一個關於版本的問題，但現場沒有可核對的資料。我們先記下需要甚麼，下次帶版本頁來，再繼續今天已準備的段落吧。

examples.en: Since this edition question has cropped up without the relevant pages available, could we keep a note for the next meeting? We can compare those pages then and return now to the passage everyone has prepared.
examples.zh: 既然出現了版本問題，而相關頁面不在手邊，我們可否先記下，留待下次聚會？到時可以比較那些頁面，現在先回到大家準備好的段落。

glossary.en: keep a note for the next meeting

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出現場可說的跟進提議，分清問題已出現與答案待核；指定下次比較版本頁，並保留今天可繼續的討論。

takeaways.en: An unexpected funding question cropped up near the end, so the chair recorded it for the next discussion.
takeaways.zh: 接近結束時，出現一個未預期的經費問題，主席便記下，留待下次討論。

takeaways.en: The old studio’s name keeps cropping up in the interviews, giving the researcher several accounts to compare.
takeaways.zh: 舊工作室的名字在訪問中不斷出現，讓研究者有幾份敘述可比較。

brief.meaningEn: Machines can perform the physical effort in a task while other parts may still require people.
brief.meaningZh: 把肌肉代指體力，描述機器可接手任務中的體力部分，其他部分仍可能需要人。
brief.grammar: Machines may/can/could replace the muscle in a process. Muscle stands for physical effort, not every role of the worker; modal verbs indicate possibility rather than a completed replacement.
brief.register: A contextual body-for-labour metaphor, not a fixed prediction about jobs or an established whole-clause idiom. Identify the actual operation and remaining judgement.
brief.boundaryZh: 體力部分可由機器處理，不等於整份工作已不需要人，也不等於所有場地都已裝備相同工具。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把可能性寫成已發生，也不要因仍需有人監察，就說機器完全沒有減輕體力工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清體力操作、其他責任及尚未測試的條件。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Machines may replace the muscle while workers handle decisions.

listening.en: Machines may replace the muscle in moving the stage panels, if the powered trolley fits the doorway. Our crew would still plan the route and check the panels; we have not tried the trolley in that hall yet.
listening.zh: 如果電動手推車能通過門口，機器可能接手搬舞台板的體力部分。團隊仍要規劃路線及核對板件；我們還未在那個大堂試過車。
listening.promptZh: 哪些部分可能改變？甚麼還未確定？

options.en: The trolley may handle physical movement, but doorway fit remains untested and people still have planning duties.
options.zh: 手推車可能處理搬運，但能否過門仍未測試，人也仍有規劃責任。

options.en: The crew has already moved every panel through the doorway using the trolley.
options.zh: 團隊已用手推車把每塊板搬過門口。

options.en: The crew had already checked the doorway before proposing this use of the trolley.
options.zh: 團隊提出這個手推車方案前，已核對過門口。

options.en: The proposal replaces route planning rather than the effort of moving the panels.
options.zh: 建議取代的是路線規劃，不是搬動板件的體力。

listening.explanationZh: 這是有條件的可能方案，還未在場地試用；搬運與路線規劃是不同部分。

reply.promptEn: What change are you considering for the stage-panel move?
reply.promptZh: 你們正考慮怎樣改搬板安排？

options.en: Machines may replace the muscle if the trolley fits, while we retain the route and panel checks.
options.zh: 如果手推車適用，機器可能接手體力部分，我們仍保留路線及板件核對。

options.en: We are considering powered help with carrying rather than removing the crew’s judgement.
options.zh: 我們考慮用動力工具協助搬運，不是取消團隊判斷。

options.en: The proposal separates the lifting effort from the planning people would still do.
options.zh: 建議把提搬的體力，與人仍須做的規劃分開。

options.en: We want to test whether the doorway allows a tool to reduce the carrying work.
options.zh: 我們想測試門口是否容許工具減輕搬運工作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述仍在考慮的體力替代方案，沒有把試用或規劃說成已完成。

scene.promptZh: 倉庫已用機械把箱子升到工作枱，但職員仍逐件判斷哪些包裝需要重封。評論只因人仍要判斷，就說機械沒有接手任何體力部分。哪句最好？

options.en: Machines can replace the muscle involved in lifting while people still judge the packaging.
options.zh: 機器可以接手提升箱子的體力部分，同時由人判斷包裝。

options.en: The remaining judgement shows that staff still lift every box by hand.
options.zh: 仍要判斷，顯示職員依然用手提起每個箱子。

options.en: The account says the machine decides which packages need resealing as well as lifting them.
options.zh: 敘述說機械除了提箱，也決定哪些包裝需要重封。

scene.explanationZh: 仍有人工判斷，不會抹去機械已接手提升這一部分。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「Machines may replace the muscle」確定？

options.en: 機器可能處理體力部分。
所有相關人員的工作已被全面取代。
仍應問體力部分具體是甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: may及muscle都有限定，不能擴成已完成的全面工作取代。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只要有電動車，門口和路線就不用再問了。」你們還未在大堂試過。哪句最好？

options.en: Machines may replace the muscle, but we first need to test whether this trolley fits the hall and the route we plan to use.
options.zh: 機器可能接手體力部分，但首先要測試這架車是否適合大堂及預定路線。

options.en: I assumed powered movement meant the trolley could use the same route regardless of the doorway.
options.zh: 我以為有動力，就表示無論門口怎樣，手推車都能走相同路線。

options.en: I thought keeping people to check the route meant the trolley could not reduce the carrying at all.
options.zh: 我以為保留人工核對路線，就表示手推車完全不能減少搬運。

dialogue.explanationZh: 能否使用有具體場地條件；人工規劃與減少體力工作可以並存。

speaking.en: Machines can replace the muscle in lifting the crates, but the crew still decides where each one belongs.
speaking.zh: 機器可以接手提起木箱的體力部分，但每箱應放哪裏，仍由團隊決定。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清搬運與決定物品位置的工作。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為職業體驗展寫一段工作介紹。新工具替布料工人捲起厚布，但工人仍檢查布面的色差，再決定哪卷適合訂單。用一至兩句英文寫實際介紹，讓訪客看見機械分擔及人的判斷，不斷言工人已失去工作。

examples.en: Machines can replace the muscle used to roll the heavy cloth, while the workers still examine its colour and choose what fits each order. This display shows a change in one operation, not the disappearance of the workers’ role.
examples.zh: 機器可以接手捲起厚布的體力部分，工人仍檢查顏色，再選擇適合每張訂單的布料。這個展示說明一項操作的改變，不是工人角色消失。

examples.en: In this workshop, machines may replace the muscle involved in winding cloth, but not the judgement about colour differences. The workers’ inspection connects the material with the needs of each order.
examples.zh: 在這個工場，機器可能接手捲布的體力部分，卻不是對色差的判斷。工人的檢查，把材料與每張訂單的需要連起來。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫可展示的工作介紹，指明捲布與色差檢查兩種不同工作，不把機械分擔說成整個職業已消失。

takeaways.en: Machines may replace the muscle in pulling the loaded trolley, while staff decide which deliveries should go first.
takeaways.zh: 機器可能接手拉動滿載手推車的體力部分，職員則決定先送哪批貨。

takeaways.en: The training display asks where machines can replace the muscle and which decisions still need an experienced operator.
takeaways.zh: 訓練展示請大家辨認機器可接手哪些體力部分，以及哪些決定仍需有經驗的操作者。

brief.meaningEn: Understand the conditions or social cues in a situation in order to decide how to respond.
brief.meaningZh: 理解當下條件或社交線索，以決定怎樣回應。
brief.grammar: read/reads/reading the situation; read is also past with a different pronunciation. Read the situation carefully/before responding. Understanding can be tentative and may need a question to check.
brief.register: A familiar figurative read collocation, not literal printed reading or a guarantee of knowing another person’s thoughts.
brief.boundaryZh: 觀察可以支持初步理解，但同一反應可能有不同原因；不能把自己的解讀當成對方已確認的想法。
brief.misconceptionZh: 安靜可能是思考、聽不清或不想立即回答；應按其他線索及適當提問了解。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用實際線索提出合適回應，也能分清觀察與推測。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A skilled worker can read the situation quickly.

listening.en: I tried to read the situation before asking the quiet visitor another question. She was looking towards the noisy doorway, so I asked whether a quieter spot would help rather than assume she did not want to talk.
listening.zh: 再問安靜的訪客問題前，我先嘗試判讀情況。她正望向嘈吵門口，所以我問安靜一點的位置會否有幫助，而不假定她不想談話。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣利用線索，又保留甚麼不確定？

options.en: The doorway glance prompted a question about noise, without treating silence as confirmed disinterest.
options.zh: 望向門口的動作，讓說話者詢問噪音問題，沒有把沉默確定為沒興趣。

options.en: The visitor explicitly said she wanted to end the conversation.
options.zh: 訪客明確表示想結束談話。

options.en: The speaker used the silence alone to decide the visitor was uninterested.
options.zh: 說話者單憑沉默，就判定訪客沒興趣。

options.en: The visitor had already asked for another question before the doorway was noticed.
options.zh: 說話者留意門口前，訪客已要求再問一條問題。

listening.explanationZh: 說話者用觀察提出可核對的問題，沒有把某種動作當成已確定的內心原因。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask about moving to a quieter spot?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼問是否想換個安靜位置？

options.en: I was trying to read the situation from her attention to the noisy doorway.
options.zh: 我想按她留意嘈吵門口的動作，判讀當時情況。

options.en: The glance suggested that the surroundings might be affecting the conversation.
options.zh: 那一眼顯示，環境可能影響談話。

options.en: I wanted to check a possible difficulty before assuming she did not want to speak.
options.zh: 我想先確認可能的困難，不假定她不想說話。

options.en: A question about the space let her explain what she needed.
options.zh: 詢問位置，讓她可以說明自己的需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋從線索到確認需要的做法，不宣稱已看穿對方心思。

scene.promptZh: 球隊練習中，隊長見兩人同時指向同一個接球位置，便先問他們是否理解了不同安排，再重新說明分區。哪句貼切？

options.en: She reads the situation by noticing a possible clash and checking the players’ understanding before giving a clearer instruction.
options.zh: 她留意到可能的衝突，先核對隊員理解，再給更清楚指示，藉此判讀情況。

options.en: She treats the pointing as a confirmed refusal to cooperate, without asking what either player means.
options.zh: 她不問兩人意思，就把指向同一處當成已確認的拒絕合作。

options.en: The account says the captain continued with the same instruction without noticing the overlap.
options.zh: 敘述說隊長沒有留意位置重疊，繼續使用相同指示。

scene.explanationZh: 留意位置重疊，再詢問理解，是把線索與回應連起來；不是先替人指定動機。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「He read the situation carefully」確定？

options.en: 他曾仔細理解當時條件。
他對每個人的動機都已得到本人確認。
可以追問他留意了哪些線索。

contrast.explanationZh: 仔細判讀不等於已確認所有人的動機，仍需看資料及提問。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「訪客沒有回答，就直接說她不感興趣吧？」你看到她正望向嘈吵門口。哪句最好？

options.en: I want to read the situation before deciding that; let me ask whether the noise is making it hard to hear.
options.zh: 決定之前，我想先判讀情況；讓我問問噪音是否令她聽不清。

options.en: I thought a pause in answering was enough to establish that the subject did not interest her.
options.zh: 我以為停下沒有回答，已足以確定她對話題沒興趣。

options.en: I would repeat the question more quickly rather than check whether she can hear it.
options.zh: 我會更快重複問題，不先問她是否聽清楚。

dialogue.explanationZh: 用具體線索提出問題，比把沉默直接當成沒興趣，或只加快問題更合適。

speaking.en: Before I answer, I want to read the situation and ask which part of the instruction is still unclear.
speaking.zh: 回答前，我想先判讀情況，再問指示中哪部分仍不清楚。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把判讀與可以核對的問題連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在社團活動後寫觀察筆記。一位新成員一直看時間，後來說要趕最後一班巴士；你原先以為他嫌討論無聊。用一至兩句英文記下你怎樣修正解讀，並提出下次先問離開時間，而不把看鐘固定解成某種態度。

examples.en: I need to read the situation more carefully: his glances at the clock concerned the last bus, not the boredom I had assumed. Next time I will ask about departure times before interpreting a hurried look as a judgement on the discussion.
examples.zh: 我需要更仔細判讀情況：他看鐘是因為最後一班巴士，不是我原先以為的無聊。下次我會先問離開時間，不把匆忙的神情直接當成對討論的評價。

examples.en: When I tried to read the situation, I mistook checking the time for a lack of interest. His explanation about the bus changed that reading, and I will ask earlier about travel constraints at the next meeting.
examples.zh: 我嘗試判讀情況時，把看時間誤解為沒興趣。他解釋巴士安排後，我修正了理解，下次聚會也會更早詢問交通限制。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫實際觀察及修正，指明巴士資料怎樣推翻原先猜測，也提出下次可問的安排；不把一種表情固定等同沒興趣。

takeaways.en: The tutor paused to read the situation when several learners began comparing different versions of the instructions.
takeaways.zh: 幾位學員開始比較不同版本的指示時，導師先停下判讀情況。

takeaways.en: She reads the situation carefully, but still asks people to confirm what they need before changing the arrangement.
takeaways.zh: 她仔細判讀情況，但改安排前仍請大家確認需要甚麼。

brief.meaningEn: Help someone feel comfortable or less worried in a situation.
brief.meaningZh: 幫人於某個情境感到自在或減少擔心。
brief.grammar: put someone at ease; put is also past, putting in progress. The object names who feels more comfortable. Explain how the action helps; it does not require agreement with every request.
brief.register: Established causative idiom, related feel more at ease as a state comparison. Being welcomed can reduce unease without removing all difficulties.
brief.boundaryZh: 讓人自在不等於替人答應一切，也不表示對方從此沒有疑問；要看實際回應及本人感受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能單從笑容或安靜就確定緊張已消失；清楚說明及容許發問也可以幫人自在。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出具體接待做法，並尊重對方選擇及仍可詢問的需要。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The host knew how to put people at ease.

listening.en: The host put the newcomers at ease by showing where to leave their bags and saying they could listen before joining the game. Two people still asked about the rules, and she welcomed those questions.
listening.zh: 主持告訴新來的人可以在哪裏放袋，也說可先聽再加入遊戲，讓他們感到自在。仍有兩人問規則，她也歡迎那些問題。
listening.promptZh: 哪些做法有助自在？這不代表甚麼？

options.en: Clear practical guidance and a choice to listen helped, while questions were still welcome.
options.zh: 清楚實際指引及先聽的選擇有幫助，也仍歡迎發問。

options.en: The newcomers were required to play immediately before hearing any explanation.
options.zh: 新來的人被要求未聽解釋便立即參加。

options.en: Asking about the rules meant the host refused to welcome those two people.
options.zh: 有人問規則，就表示主持拒絕歡迎那兩人。

options.en: The newcomers could listen only after promising to join the next game.
options.zh: 新來的人要先答應下一局參加，才可以先聽。

listening.explanationZh: 示範具體位置及保留先聽的選擇，有助減少不確定；仍有問題也不表示接待失敗。

reply.promptEn: How did the host help the newcomers settle in?
reply.promptZh: 主持怎樣幫新來的人安頓？

options.en: She put them at ease with clear guidance and the option to listen first.
options.zh: 她給清楚指引，也讓他們可先聽，幫他們感到自在。

options.en: She explained the practical arrangements without pressing them to play at once.
options.zh: 她解釋實際安排，沒有催他們立即玩。

options.en: People knew where their bags could go and how they could begin gradually.
options.zh: 大家知道可以在哪裏放袋，也知道可逐步開始。

options.en: Her welcome included questions rather than making everyone pretend to know the rules.
options.zh: 她的接待容許發問，不要求每人假裝已懂規則。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各自交代接待如何減少不確定，沒有把自在等同不再發問。

scene.promptZh: 攝影師想用玩笑讓一位女受訪者放鬆。對方禮貌地笑了，隨後卻說自己仍很緊張，希望先暫停拍攝。旁人只因看見笑容，就判定對方已自在。哪句較準確？

options.en: The smile alone does not show that the joke put her at ease; she explicitly said she was still nervous and asked for a pause.
options.zh: 單憑笑容，不能說明玩笑已讓她自在；她明說仍緊張，也要求暫停。

options.en: Her smile confirms that she accepted the photographer’s plan to continue immediately.
options.zh: 她的笑容確認，她接受攝影師立即繼續的安排。

options.en: Her request is described as a wish to repeat the joke rather than pause the photography.
options.zh: 敘述把她的請求，描述為想再聽一次玩笑，而不是暫停拍攝。

scene.explanationZh: 應聽受訪者本人交代的感受及暫停請求，不由攝影師的好意或一個禮貌笑容，取代她的意思。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「She put me at ease」推論？

options.en: 她幫我感到較舒服或較少擔心。
我已同意她之後提出的每一項要求。
可以再說明她做了甚麼令我自在。

contrast.explanationZh: 感到自在與同意要求不同，不能替對方預先作出承諾。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「接待得好，就不用再問他們有沒有問題吧？」你知道仍有兩人想了解規則。哪句最好？

options.en: We can put people at ease and still invite questions; feeling welcome need not mean knowing every rule already.
options.zh: 我們可以讓人自在，也繼續邀請發問；感到受歡迎，不等於已知道每條規則。

options.en: I assumed a comfortable welcome meant everyone had understood the rules without asking.
options.zh: 我以為接待讓人舒服，就表示每人不用問也已懂規則。

options.en: I would explain only where the bags go and leave the remaining questions until after the game.
options.zh: 我會只說放袋的位置，把其餘問題留到遊戲後。

dialogue.explanationZh: 接待的自在感與規則理解可以分開跟進，不能用其中一項代替另一項。

speaking.en: A clear explanation can put people at ease, while leaving them free to ask whether the activity suits them.
speaking.zh: 清楚解釋可以讓人自在，同時仍讓他們自由詢問活動是否適合自己。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留自在與自行選擇的空間。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替一次初次求職訪談寫給面試者的事前訊息。你可以告知地點、時間及可問清楚問題，但不能保證獲聘。用一至兩句英文實際提供到場資料：周三十時、圖書館樓上的會議室；若問題不清楚，可請面試官重說。讓人安心而不假裝已有結果。

examples.en: To put you at ease before Wednesday’s interview, we will meet at ten in the meeting room above the library. If a question is unclear, please ask us to repeat it.
examples.zh: 為了讓你在周三面試前感到自在，我們會在十時於圖書館樓上的會議室見面。如果問題不清楚，請我們重說即可。

examples.en: I hope these details put you at ease: your interview is at ten on Wednesday in the room above the library. You are welcome to ask for a question to be repeated.
examples.zh: 希望這些資料讓你感到自在：面試在周三十時，地點是圖書館樓上的房間。歡迎你請我們重說問題。

glossary.en: the meeting room above the library
ask for a question to be repeated

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫具體、可直接寄出的會面資料及發問安排，準確保留周三十時和圖書館樓上的地點，不把安心說成保證獲聘。

takeaways.en: The librarian put me at ease by explaining that I could ask about the catalogue before choosing a book.
takeaways.zh: 圖書館員解釋，我可以先問目錄怎樣用，再選書，讓我感到自在。

takeaways.en: A friendly introduction put the visitor at ease, but she still wanted time to decide whether to join the workshop.
takeaways.zh: 友善介紹讓訪客感到自在，但她仍想有時間決定是否參加工作坊。

brief.meaningEn: Make the atmosphere or someone’s emotional state happier or more positive.
brief.meaningZh: 讓現場氣氛或某人的心情變得愉快、較正面。
brief.grammar: lift/lifted/lifting the mood; lift the mood in a room/of a group. Describe the observed change without assuming every person felt the same or that practical problems disappeared.
brief.register: A common upward-movement metaphor. A lighter mood is not necessarily motivation to take on work, and a temporary change need not settle a disagreement.
brief.boundaryZh: 氣氛好轉與問題解決不同，也不能由一人發笑推斷每人的感受；要交代可觀察的變化及範圍。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把幽默當成人人都需要的回應；對方若想嚴肅談問題，仍須聆聽。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體描述氣氛的變化，同時不掩蓋仍待處理的事情。

sources.sentence: Her calm joke helped lift the mood.

listening.en: The shared photograph lifted the mood after a tiring rehearsal: several people laughed at the old costumes and began talking again. We still had to resolve the missing prop, so the lighter atmosphere was not the end of the work.
listening.zh: 辛苦排練後，一張共看的舊照片讓氣氛好轉：幾人看見舊服裝笑起來，又開始談話。我們仍要處理遺失道具，所以氣氛輕鬆些，不表示工作已完。
listening.promptZh: 哪些事改變了？甚麼仍未處理？

options.en: Some people laughed and resumed talking, while the missing prop still needed attention.
options.zh: 有些人笑起來，重新談話，但遺失道具仍須處理。

options.en: The photograph showed where the missing prop had already been stored.
options.zh: 照片顯示遺失道具已存放在哪裏。

options.en: Everyone left as soon as the photograph appeared, without further conversation.
options.zh: 照片一出現，大家就離開，沒有再談話。

options.en: The group laughed about the prop having been recovered before they looked at the photograph.
options.zh: 小組看照片前，已因道具找回來而笑起來。

listening.explanationZh: 照片中的舊服裝帶來笑聲及重新談話；敘述仍說道具未處理，不是先找回道具才看照片。

reply.promptEn: What effect did sharing the photograph have?
reply.promptZh: 分享照片有甚麼作用？

options.en: It lifted the mood by giving some of us a lighter moment after the rehearsal.
options.zh: 它讓部分人在排練後輕鬆一點，改善了氣氛。

options.en: People who had been tired began laughing and talking about the costumes.
options.zh: 原本疲累的人開始笑着談舊服裝。

options.en: The room became more sociable without the prop question being resolved.
options.zh: 大家較願意談話，但道具問題並沒有解決。

options.en: It changed the immediate atmosphere rather than completing the practical work.
options.zh: 它改變眼前的氣氛，不是完成實際工作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都分清氣氛變化與實務結果，沒有替全體指定相同心情。

scene.promptZh: 團隊收到很難處理的改期消息，主持先問大家最擔心甚麼，現場仍然嚴肅；沒有人描述心情好轉。旁人只因主持很親切，就說已讓氣氛變愉快。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: A considerate response may help, but this account does not yet show that it lifted the mood.
options.zh: 體貼的回應可能有幫助，但這份敘述還未顯示氣氛已變愉快。

options.en: The account reports that everyone laughed and relaxed after the question.
options.zh: 敘述表示，提問後每人都笑起來並放鬆。

options.en: Asking about worries establishes a happier atmosphere even without any response from the group.
options.zh: 即使未有小組回應，詢問擔心也足以確定氣氛較愉快。

scene.explanationZh: 可以肯定願意了解，但氣氛變化仍要有資料，不能只按主持人的意圖判斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「The joke lifted the mood」推論？

options.en: 笑話讓氣氛或心情好轉。
原本的分歧已獲每人接受的解決方案。
可以再了解哪些反應顯示好轉。

contrast.explanationZh: 心情變化與分歧是否解決不同，後者需要另外的資訊。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「看完照片大家又有精神說話了，接着怎樣？」你想趁休息先商量仍缺的道具，再繼續排練。哪句最清楚？

options.en: The photograph lifted the mood; let us use the break to discuss the missing prop before we resume the rehearsal.
options.zh: 照片改善了氣氛；我們趁休息先談遺失道具，再繼續排練吧。

options.en: I would resume the rehearsal first and leave the prop discussion until we have finished the next run.
options.zh: 我會先繼續排練，等下一次全段排完後才談道具。

options.en: I would keep looking through the photographs for now and wait for someone else to bring up the prop.
options.zh: 我會暫時繼續看照片，等別人先提道具的事。

dialogue.explanationZh: 說話者想趁休息先討論仍缺的道具，再回到排練；先排完或等別人開口，都沒有清楚落實這個安排。

speaking.en: The music lifted the mood during the break, although the team still needed a serious conversation about the next deadline.
speaking.zh: 休息時，音樂讓氣氛好轉，但團隊仍需要認真談下一個期限。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留氣氛好轉與後續嚴肅討論的分別。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替一場停電後重新開放的社區活動寫回顧。現場播放舊歌，有幾人開始哼唱，但你還沒問較遠座位的參加者，也不知道有人是否仍不安。用一至兩句英文寫實際回顧，限定在觀察到的部分，不宣布所有人已開心或停電影響已消失。

examples.en: The old songs appeared to lift the mood near the front, where several people began humming after the power returned. We have not yet heard from people in the farther seats, so this is only part of the room’s experience.
examples.zh: 恢復供電後，前排幾人開始哼舊歌，歌曲看來讓那一帶的氣氛好轉。我們還未聽較遠座位的人怎樣說，所以這只是現場部分人的經驗。

examples.en: Several people hummed along, suggesting that the music helped lift the mood after the interruption. Their response does not tell us how everyone felt, and we still need to ask those seated farther away.
examples.zh: 幾人跟着哼唱，顯示音樂有助改善中斷後的氣氛。他們的回應不能說明所有人的感受，我們仍須詢問坐得較遠的人。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫有範圍的實際觀察，清楚交代哪些人有甚麼反應及還未了解誰，不把局部哼唱當成全場或所有問題的結論。

takeaways.en: The unexpected postcard lifted the mood at the table, and the group spent a few minutes recalling the trip.
takeaways.zh: 意外收到的明信片讓桌邊氣氛好轉，大家花了幾分鐘回想旅程。

takeaways.en: Her warm introduction helped lift the mood before the meeting, without promising agreement on the difficult proposal.
takeaways.zh: 她溫暖的介紹有助在會前改善氣氛，但沒有保證大家會同意那個困難提案。

target.pattern: \bmake(?:s)? the room feel heavy\b|\bmade the room feel heavy\b

brief.meaningEn: Create a tense, oppressive or subdued emotional atmosphere, using weight as a contextual image.
brief.meaningZh: 以重量比喻，使現場情緒氣氛變得緊張、壓抑或低沉。
brief.grammar: make/makes/made the room feel heavy; a remark can make the room feel heavy. The room stands for the atmosphere among the people, not a physical increase in mass.
brief.register: Contextual weight metaphor rather than a separately fixed idiom. Describe the actual behaviour and perspective; a quiet room is not automatically a distressed one.
brief.boundaryZh: 安靜或認真不一定是壓抑，要看反應及上下文；這個描述也不證明所有人都有相同感受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因事情嚴肅，就說氣氛惡化；同樣，笑聲也不自動代表沒有壓力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體反應描述沉重氣氛，也能詢問觀察範圍之外的感受。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: One bitter remark can make the room feel heavy.

listening.en: The sarcastic comment made the room feel heavy: two members stopped offering ideas, and the next speaker hesitated. I described how it felt from my seat, not what every person in the room was thinking.
listening.zh: 那句挖苦的話讓現場氣氛沉重：兩位成員不再提想法，下一位說話者也猶豫了。我描述的是自己座位上的感受，不是全場每人的想法。
listening.promptZh: 哪些反應支持描述？說話者保留甚麼範圍？

options.en: Reduced participation and hesitation supported the speaker’s impression, without establishing everyone’s thoughts.
options.zh: 較少參與及猶豫支持說話者的感受，但沒有確定每人的想法。

options.en: Everyone openly agreed that the comment had improved the discussion.
options.zh: 每人都公開同意，那句話改善了討論。

options.en: The speaker interviewed every participant before describing a shared reaction.
options.zh: 說話者先訪問每位參加者，才描述共同反應。

options.en: The two members stopped speaking because their scheduled presentations had already ended.
options.zh: 兩位成員因已完成排定的演講，才停止說話。

listening.explanationZh: 不再提想法及猶豫是具體線索，但說話者明確沒有替每人報告內心。

reply.promptEn: Why did you describe the atmosphere as oppressive?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把氣氛形容為壓抑？

options.en: The sarcastic comment made the room feel heavy as people withdrew from offering ideas.
options.zh: 挖苦的話讓人退縮，不再提想法，使現場氣氛沉重。

options.en: The change in participation and the next speaker’s hesitation affected how the room felt to me.
options.zh: 參與方式的改變及下一位的猶豫，影響了我對氣氛的感受。

options.en: I noticed less willingness to contribute after the remark.
options.zh: 那句話之後，我留意到大家較不願意提出意見。

options.en: The withdrawal and hesitation supported that impression, though they did not tell me what everyone was thinking.
options.zh: 退縮及猶豫支持那種感受，但沒有告訴我每人在想甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都把描述連到具體互動，不把個人觀察誇成全體已確認的反應。

scene.promptZh: 學生安靜地看一段複雜資料，之後輪流提出切題問題，也說有足夠時間思考。旁人只因沒人立即說話，就判定氣氛壓抑。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Silence alone does not show that anything made the room feel heavy; the account describes attentive thinking and useful questions.
options.zh: 沉默本身不顯示有事情令氣氛沉重；敘述描述專注思考及有用問題。

options.en: The students’ silence is given as confirmation that they felt unable to contribute.
options.zh: 學生沉默，被列為他們覺得無法參與的確認。

options.en: The account reports that no student asked a relevant question afterwards.
options.zh: 敘述表示，之後沒有學生問切題問題。

scene.explanationZh: 要分清專注思考與受壓而退縮；題目有之後積極提問的資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「His remark made the room feel heavy」推論？

options.en: 說話者把話後的氣氛描述為沉重。
每位在場者已親口確認同一種感受。
可以再問有哪些反應支持描述。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個圖像沒有提供所有人的回應，也不是全體情緒的量度。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「兩人沒再提想法，就直接寫每個人都害怕他吧？」你只知道自己的觀察。哪句最好？

options.en: The comment made the room feel heavy to me, but I should ask others how they felt before describing everyone’s reaction.
options.zh: 我覺得那句話讓氣氛沉重，但描述全體反應前，應先問其他人的感受。

options.en: I thought two people’s silence was enough to establish that everyone felt afraid of the speaker.
options.zh: 我以為兩人沉默，已足以確定每人都怕那位說話者。

options.en: I would treat the lack of an immediate objection as agreement that the comment was harmless.
options.zh: 我會把沒有立即反對，當成大家同意那句話沒有影響。

dialogue.explanationZh: 既不把兩人反應擴成全體恐懼，也不把未反對當成沒受影響；需要再聽本人怎樣說。

speaking.en: An unexplained criticism can make the room feel heavy, so I would rather describe the work clearly than judge the person.
speaking.zh: 沒有解釋的批評可能讓現場氣氛沉重，所以我寧願清楚描述作品，而不是評斷人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清對作品的具體回饋與對人的評斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為一齣短劇寫觀後短評。最後一幕播放主角已故姐姐留下的告別錄音，人物流淚，觀眾也安靜了片刻；你自己覺得沉重，而這正呼應作品的哀悼主題。用一至兩句英文寫可刊出的短評，不把沉重直接當作演出失敗，也不替所有觀眾說出同一感受。

examples.en: The recorded farewell seemed to make the room feel heavy, with the characters in tears and a pause before the audience responded. For me, that weight served the play’s mourning theme rather than showing that the performance had failed.
examples.zh: 告別錄音看來讓現場氣氛沉重：人物流淚，觀眾也停頓片刻才有回應。對我而言，這份沉重呼應作品的哀悼主題，不是演出失敗的證明。

examples.en: The sister’s farewell made the room feel heavy to me, especially during the silence after the recording. I read that moment as part of the play’s mourning, while leaving other audience members free to describe their own responses.
examples.zh: 姐姐的告別讓我覺得現場氣氛沉重，尤其是錄音之後的沉默。我把那一刻理解為作品哀悼的一部分，也保留其他觀眾說出自己回應的空間。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交付短劇評論，以告別錄音及具體反應解釋自己的感受，把沉重連到哀悼主題，不用單一情緒判定演出成敗或全場感受。

takeaways.en: The unexplained rejection made the room feel heavy, and the chair asked people to describe their concerns before continuing.
takeaways.zh: 沒有解釋的否決讓氣氛沉重，主席便請大家先說擔心甚麼，再繼續。

takeaways.en: A personal insult can make the room feel heavy even when the original disagreement concerns only a small design choice.
takeaways.zh: 即使原本只在討論一個小設計選擇，人身侮辱也可能讓現場氣氛沉重。

target.pattern: \bdrain(?:s|ed|ing)? the air out of (?:it|the discussion|the meeting|the dinner scene)\b

brief.meaningEn: Remove the liveliness or positive energy from a previously named activity, as if letting air out of something inflated.
brief.meaningZh: 把原本活動中的活力或正面氣氛比作被放掉的空氣，描述它減少或消失。
brief.grammar: drain the air out of it/the discussion; drained/draining. It needs a clear antecedent. Explain which response or event reduced the energy; this expanded wording is a contextual image.
brief.register: Creative deflation metaphor retained from the supplied example, not taught as a separately fixed dictionary idiom. It concerns emotional energy rather than ventilation.
brief.boundaryZh: 氣氛低落不代表每個人都一樣，也不會自動說明說話者的動機；要分清效果、觀察及意圖。
brief.misconceptionZh: 短暫安靜未必是失去活力，可能有人正在思考；需要實際前後反應支持。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體線索解釋活力的變化，不把形象比喻當成動機的證據。

sources.expression: drain the air out of it
sources.sentence: One bitter comment can drain the air out of it.

listening.en: The discussion had been lively until a member dismissed the ideas as pointless. The comment seemed to drain the air out of it: people stopped building on each other’s suggestions, though we did not ask how everyone felt.
listening.zh: 討論原本活躍，直到一位成員把想法說成毫無意義。那句話看來讓活力洩掉：大家不再接着別人的建議發展，但我們沒有問每人的感受。
listening.promptZh: 前後有甚麼變化？哪些資料仍未掌握？

options.en: Ideas stopped developing together after the dismissal, but individual feelings were not checked.
options.zh: 否定之後，大家不再一起發展想法，但個人感受未經詢問。

options.en: Every participant confirmed feeling cheerful immediately after the comment.
options.zh: 每位參加者都確認，那句話之後立即感到高興。

options.en: The discussion became lively only after the ideas had been dismissed.
options.zh: 想法被否定之後，討論才變得活躍。

options.en: The speaker describes a planned silent writing period before sharing more suggestions.
options.zh: 說話者描述原定先安靜寫作，再分享更多建議的時段。

listening.explanationZh: 不再互相延伸建議是可觀察的轉變，但沒有個別回應，就不能代每人報告心情。

reply.promptEn: Why did you use an image of losing air for the discussion?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼用洩氣的意象形容討論？

options.en: The dismissal seemed to drain the air out of it as people stopped developing the suggestions together.
options.zh: 否定之後，大家不再一起發展建議，彷彿讓討論的活力洩掉。

options.en: The earlier flow of ideas weakened after the remark.
options.zh: 那句話之後，原本流動的想法減少了。

options.en: People no longer added to one another’s contributions in the way they had before.
options.zh: 大家不再像之前那樣延伸別人的意見。

options.en: People had been building on the ideas and then stopped, suggesting lost energy rather than a report from every person.
options.zh: 大家原本接着想法發展，之後卻停下，顯示活力減少，不是每人親口報告的感受。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都把意象連到互動前後的變化，並保留觀察範圍。

scene.promptZh: 小組按主持要求安靜畫三分鐘，之後每人提出新想法，並熱烈比較。有人只看畫圖時沒人說話，就稱討論洩了氣。哪句較準確？

options.zh: 原定的安靜時段，不顯示有事情令討論洩氣；之後的交流很活躍。

options.en: The account describes members losing interest and refusing to share their drawings.
options.zh: 敘述描述成員失去興趣，拒絕分享畫作。

options.en: The three quiet minutes replaced the planned comparison, which never happened.
options.zh: 三分鐘的安靜取代了原定比較，之後並沒有比較。

scene.explanationZh: 需要看整段安排及後續互動，不能單從暫時安靜推斷活力消失。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「The comment seemed to drain the air out of it」確定？

options.en: 說話者感到那句話令活動失去活力。
發言者已承認，自己故意讓大家難過。
需要知道it指甚麼活動或情境。

contrast.explanationZh: seemed及意象描述效果，不證明動機，更沒有報告對方已承認意圖。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「氣氛受影響，就寫他故意打擊每個人吧？」你只有前後互動的觀察。哪句最好？

options.en: The remark seemed to drain the air out of the discussion, but its effect does not establish what he intended.
options.zh: 那句話看來令討論的活力洩掉，但效果不能確定他的意圖。

options.en: I assumed a negative effect on the group was enough to confirm a deliberate attempt to hurt them.
options.zh: 我以為對小組有負面效果，已足以確認他故意傷害大家。

options.en: I thought we had checked everyone’s feelings because we noticed fewer suggestions.
options.zh: 我以為留意到建議減少，就表示已問過每人的感受。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可描述互動轉變，同時分清尚未了解的動機及個人感受。

speaking.en: The abrupt reply appeared to drain the air out of the meeting, but I would ask what people experienced before speaking for them.
speaking.zh: 突兀的回覆看來讓會議洩了氣，但代表別人說話前，我會先問他們的經驗。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把觀察與代別人發言的界線分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說短評。原文把一場熱鬧家宴寫得充滿說笑，叔叔一句「還是別提了」後，敘述轉向停下的筷子和沒再回應的客人，卻沒有交代叔叔內心。用一至兩句英文分析這個敘事轉折，依據細節而不斷定叔叔故意傷人。

examples.en: The brief reply seems to drain the air out of the dinner scene, as the narration moves from jokes to still chopsticks and unanswered remarks. Those details suggest a loss of energy without telling us what the uncle intended.
examples.zh: 簡短回覆看來讓家宴場面的活力洩掉，因敘述從笑話轉向停下的筷子及沒有回應的話。那些細節顯示活力減少，卻沒有告訴我們叔叔的意圖。

examples.en: The writer lets one reply drain the air out of it: the lively dinner becomes a scene of paused eating and broken conversation. This is an effect created through the narrated details, not direct access to the uncle’s thoughts.
examples.zh: 作者用一句回覆讓家宴洩了氣：熱鬧晚飯變成停下進食、對話中斷的場面。這是敘事細節造成的效果，不是讓讀者直接看見叔叔的想法。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫小說短評，以敘述細節說明氣氛轉折，分清文本效果及未交代的人物內心，不把讀者感受當成角色已承認的動機。

takeaways.en: The unqualified rejection seemed to drain the air out of the discussion before the group had explored the idea.
takeaways.zh: 小組還未探索想法，毫無解釋的否決看來已讓討論洩了氣。

takeaways.en: She worried that dismissing the questions as trivial would drain the air out of the meeting.
takeaways.zh: 她擔心，把問題當成瑣碎而不理，會讓會議失去活力。

brief.meaningEn: The prevailing emotional atmosphere within a group or setting, shaped by patterns of interaction.
brief.meaningZh: 群體或環境中較普遍的情緒氛圍，由互動方式等因素形成。
brief.grammar: the emotional climate in/of a group; shape/change the emotional climate. Climate is figurative here; evidence may include repeated interactions and people’s accounts, not one universal feeling.
brief.register: A familiar climate-as-atmosphere metaphor. It can describe welcoming, anxious or mixed conditions without diagnosing individuals or attributing everything to one leader.
brief.boundaryZh: 群體氛圍不等於每個人感受完全相同，也不能只靠一張照片或一次反應概括長期相處。
brief.misconceptionZh: 形容氛圍時應交代時間、觀察及資料來源，不把個人心情當成整個小組的情況。
brief.outcomeZh: 能查問及描述互動氛圍，保留不同成員的經驗。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A leader helps shape the emotional climate.

listening.en: Over several meetings, the emotional climate changed as members began admitting mistakes without being mocked. Two newcomers said they felt safer asking questions, though we still needed to hear from the quieter members.
listening.zh: 幾次會議下來，成員開始能承認錯誤而不被嘲笑，情緒氛圍也改變了。兩位新成員說較敢發問，但我們仍需聽較安靜成員的經驗。
listening.promptZh: 描述氛圍改變用了哪些資料？還有誰未被了解？

options.en: Repeated changes in interaction and two members’ accounts, with quieter members still to be heard.
options.zh: 幾次互動的改變及兩位成員的敘述，較安靜成員則仍待了解。

options.en: One photograph that establishes the feelings of everyone over the whole year.
options.zh: 一張足以確定全體整年感受的照片。

options.en: A report that no member had asked a question during any meeting.
options.zh: 一份表示任何會議都沒有人發問的報告。

options.en: Confirmation that the quieter members had the same experience before anyone asked them.
options.zh: 未詢問較安靜成員，就已確認他們有相同經驗。

listening.explanationZh: 資料有一段時間內的互動及本人敘述，但不能替尚未回應的成員作結論。

reply.promptEn: What suggests that the group’s atmosphere was changing?
reply.promptZh: 甚麼顯示小組的氛圍正在改變？

options.en: The emotional climate became more accepting of mistakes across several meetings.
options.zh: 幾次會議下來，情緒氛圍變得較接納錯誤。

options.en: People could acknowledge an error without the mocking that would discourage questions.
options.zh: 大家可以承認錯誤，不必面對令人不敢發問的嘲笑。

options.en: Two newcomers described feeling more able to ask questions.
options.zh: 兩位新成員說，自己較敢提出問題。

options.en: The observed interactions and the newcomers’ accounts point in a similar direction.
options.zh: 觀察到的互動與新成員的敘述，指向相近的變化。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各自用互動或已取得的敘述回答，不把未回應者也當成已確認。

scene.promptZh: 一張宣傳照片裏，五人都笑着；文章沒有問他們平日是否敢提出不同意見，就稱小組全年都很開放。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: A smiling photograph alone does not establish the emotional climate across a year of meetings.
options.zh: 單靠一張笑着的照片，不足以確定全年會議中的情緒氛圍。

options.en: The photograph documents how members responded to disagreement throughout the year.
options.zh: 照片記錄了成員全年怎樣回應分歧。

options.en: The account includes each member’s explanation of how freely they can question a proposal.
options.zh: 敘述包括每位成員說明，自己能多自由地質疑提案。

scene.explanationZh: 一次拍照反應不等於長期互動資料，尤其沒有涉及如何處理分歧。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「The emotional climate has improved」推論？

options.en: 某個群體的情緒氛圍被描述為改善。
每位成員已親口表示沒有任何擔心。
可以再問哪些互動及經驗支持描述。

contrast.explanationZh: 整體描述不等於取得全體相同回應，更不會證明所有擔心消失。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「兩位新人覺得自在，就不用問安靜的人吧？」你想了解更多經驗。哪句最好？

options.en: Their accounts help us understand the emotional climate, but we should also invite the quieter members to describe what participation feels like for them.
options.zh: 他們的敘述有助理解情緒氛圍，但也應邀較安靜成員說明自己參與時的感受。

options.en: I assumed two positive accounts were enough to establish the same experience for everyone.
options.zh: 我以為兩份正面敘述，已足以確定每人有相同經驗。

options.en: I would use the number of questions alone, without asking whether people felt able to disagree.
options.zh: 我會只看問題數量，不問大家是否覺得可以提出分歧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以保留正面資料，也繼續了解不同參與方式，不能用回應數量代替感受內容。

speaking.en: I want to understand the emotional climate by asking how people respond when someone changes their mind.
speaking.zh: 我想問大家怎樣回應別人改變想法，藉此了解情緒氛圍。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把抽象氛圍連到具體互動。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫攝影會學期報告。匿名回饋顯示，三位成員覺得休息時容易聊天，卻不敢在正式評作品時提出分歧；兩人則說正式討論也自在。下學期你提議評作品前先給大家幾分鐘寫意見。用一至兩句英文寫實際報告段落，保留不同經驗，並提出這項可試的改變。

examples.en: The feedback suggests a mixed emotional climate: three members find break-time chats comfortable but hesitate to disagree during formal critiques, while two feel at ease there too. Next term, we propose a few minutes of written reflection before each critique.
examples.zh: 回饋顯示情緒氛圍並不一致：三位成員覺得休息聊天自在，正式評作品時卻不敢提出分歧；另兩人在正式討論也自在。下學期，我們提議每次評作品前，先留幾分鐘書面整理意見。

examples.en: Our report distinguishes the emotional climate of informal breaks from that of formal critiques, with three members reporting difficulty disagreeing and two describing comfort in both settings. We will try a short period for writing comments before next term’s critiques.
examples.zh: 報告把非正式休息與正式評作品的情緒氛圍分開：三位成員說難以在正式場合提出分歧，兩位則說兩種場合都自在。下學期評作品前，我們會試行短暫書面整理意見的時間。

glossary.en: a short period for writing comments
glossary.zh: 一段寫意見的短暫時間

writing.selfCheckZh: 交付有根據的學期報告，保留三人與兩人的不同回饋，分清場合，再提出先寫意見的試行安排，不先宣布已改善。

takeaways.en: The editor asked how the emotional climate affected newcomers’ willingness to offer unfinished ideas.
takeaways.zh: 編輯問，情緒氛圍怎樣影響新成員提出未完成想法的意願。

takeaways.en: Their report described a mixed emotional climate, with friendly breaks but tense discussions about mistakes.
takeaways.zh: 報告描述一種混合的情緒氛圍：休息時友善，討論錯誤時卻緊張。

lessons.titleZh: 不自然或不真誠的笑容

brief.meaningEn: A smile presented as artificial or insincere rather than genuinely expressing pleasure.
brief.meaningZh: 把笑容形容為不自然或不真誠，而不是真正流露愉快。
brief.grammar: wear/give/describe a plastic smile. Plastic is a contextual artificiality image, not the material of the person’s face. Establish how the narrator knows the feeling or intention.
brief.register: A familiar artificiality metaphor, often critical. A still photograph or polite smile alone does not prove insincerity; nervousness and other explanations may remain.
brief.boundaryZh: 不能單憑照片或外表斷定某人虛偽；文學文本若交代內心，與旁觀者只看表情的證據不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 禮貌或緊張不自動等於欺騙，也不能因看見笑容就確定對方開心。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清文本明示的內心與現實中尚未確認的感受。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A plastic smile will not reassure a worried team.

listening.en: In the story, Mara wore a plastic smile while secretly resenting the compliment. The narrator tells us she was hiding irritation, so the description has support beyond the expression another character could see.
listening.zh: 故事裏，Mara一邊露出不真誠的笑容，一邊暗自不滿那句稱讚。敘述者告訴我們，她正在掩飾惱怒，所以描述的依據不只其他角色看見的表情。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼資料支持不真誠的描述？

options.en: The narrator explicitly identifies the irritation Mara is hiding.
options.zh: 敘述者明確交代Mara正在掩飾的惱怒。

options.en: Another character has confirmed her feelings from a photograph alone.
options.zh: 另一角色單憑照片，就已確認她的感受。

options.en: The narrator says Mara genuinely enjoys the compliment and feels no irritation.
options.zh: 敘述者說Mara真正喜歡那句稱讚，沒有不滿。

options.en: Mara has explained her irritation openly to the person praising her.
options.zh: Mara已向稱讚她的人公開解釋不滿。

listening.explanationZh: 敘述者提供內心資料，支持笑容與感受不一致；這不是單憑外表猜測。

reply.promptEn: Why is the smile described as artificial in the story?
reply.promptZh: 故事為甚麼把笑容描述為不真誠？

options.en: It is a plastic smile because the narrator says Mara is hiding irritation rather than enjoying the compliment.
options.zh: 那是不真誠的笑容，因敘述者說Mara在掩飾惱怒，不是享受稱讚。

options.en: Her shown expression does not match the feeling the narrator reveals.
options.zh: 她顯示的表情，與敘述者揭露的感受不一致。

options.en: We are told about concealed resentment, not merely shown a smiling face.
options.zh: 文本交代了隱藏的不滿，不只展示一張笑臉。

options.en: The description depends on access to her private response to the praise.
options.zh: 描述依據的是，她私下對稱讚的反應。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出文本內心資料，不把旁人看見的表情當成充分證據。

scene.promptZh: 一張頒獎照片裏，學生笑得有點僵硬；他沒有說自己的感受，也沒有其他資料。有人想直接寫他故意假裝喜歡老師。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: The photograph alone does not establish a plastic smile or the motive the observer has assigned to it.
options.zh: 單靠照片，不足以確定是不真誠的笑容，也不足以指定旁人所猜的動機。

options.en: The image records the student admitting that he dislikes the teacher.
options.zh: 照片記錄學生親口承認不喜歡老師。

options.en: A stiff expression shows that nervousness cannot explain the smile.
options.zh: 表情僵硬，顯示緊張不可能解釋那個笑容。

scene.explanationZh: 表情可以有不同原因，照片沒有提供本人感受或刻意掩飾的資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只因有人露出僵硬笑容就確定？

options.en: 可以描述照片中可見的表情。
那人心裏必定在厭惡眼前的人。
若要解釋感受，仍需要更多資料。

contrast.explanationZh: 從可見表情到指定內心厭惡，還有未經支持的推論。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然角色笑了，就不用提敘述者說她生氣吧？」你要忠於文本。哪句最好？

options.en: The narrator calls it a plastic smile precisely because the outward expression hides the irritation we are told about.
options.zh: 敘述者正因笑容掩飾已交代的惱怒，才把它稱為不真誠的笑容。

options.en: I thought any smile established pleasure even when the narrator described a conflicting feeling.
options.zh: 我以為任何笑容都能確定是愉快，即使敘述者交代了相反感受。

options.en: I assumed the other character knew about her resentment too, because the narrator had revealed it to us.
options.zh: 我以為另一個角色也知道她的不滿，因為敘述者已向我們揭露。

dialogue.explanationZh: 讀者知道外表與內心的對照，但不能假定另一角色也得到敘述者交代給讀者的內心資料。

speaking.en: The narrator describes a plastic smile, then reveals the resentment the character is trying to conceal.
speaking.zh: 敘述者描寫不真誠的笑容，再揭露角色試圖隱藏的不滿。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再交代文本怎樣提供感受的依據。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為戲劇演員寫排練便條。角色明明對失去主角位置很不滿，卻想在同伴面前表現祝賀；劇本之後才讓觀眾聽到她的獨白。用一至兩句英文提出表演安排，讓外表與獨白形成對照，不把角色的假笑當成演員本人性格。

examples.en: Could the character give a plastic smile during the congratulations, with the later monologue revealing the resentment beneath it? That contrast would belong to her role in the scene, not a judgement about you as the actor.
examples.zh: 角色祝賀時，可否露出不真誠的笑容，再由之後的獨白揭露底下的不滿？那種對照屬於她在場景中的角色，不是對你作為演員本人的判斷。

examples.en: I suggest a plastic smile for the public congratulations, followed by a more direct expression of resentment in the monologue. Please make the contrast about the character’s two responses rather than your own attitude to the other performers.
examples.zh: 我建議公開祝賀時用不真誠的笑容，獨白時再較直接地表達不滿。請把對照放在角色的兩種反應，不是你本人對其他演員的態度。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫具體排練便條，以公開祝賀與之後獨白作表演對照，清楚分開角色意圖及演員本人，不對現實人物隨意猜心思。

takeaways.en: The novel contrasts his plastic smile with the angry note he writes immediately afterwards.
takeaways.zh: 小說把他不真誠的笑容，與緊接着寫下的憤怒便條對照。

takeaways.en: She questioned the description of a plastic smile because the interview contained no account of what the person actually felt.
takeaways.zh: 她質疑不真誠笑容這個描述，因為訪問沒有交代那人實際感受。

brief.meaningEn: Make someone excited, enthusiastic or strongly motivated to act.
brief.meaningZh: 讓人興奮、有熱情，或產生強烈行動意欲。
brief.grammar: fire someone up; fire up the team; fired/firing. Pronouns go between fire and up. Fired up can describe the resulting enthusiastic state, but enthusiasm is not a completed action.
brief.register: Common informal phrasal verb for arousing energy. Context may be constructive or confrontational; name the action being encouraged rather than assume motivation is automatically good.
brief.boundaryZh: 有幹勁不等於已有技能、時間或承諾；不能只看大家叫好，就把名字列為已答應的工作人手。
brief.misconceptionZh: 也不等於實際點火；這裏要說清楚甚麼讓人想行動，以及是否已有下一步安排。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述熱情的來源，並把動機與具體參與安排分開確認。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A clear goal can fire them up.

listening.en: The clear goal fired us up: we could make the riverside path easier to use by mapping the difficult sections. We left wanting to help, but the organiser still asked us to confirm which weekend we could actually attend.
listening.zh: 清楚目標激起我們的幹勁：我們可標出難走路段，讓河邊小徑更易使用。離開時大家都想幫忙，但統籌人仍請我們確認，實際哪個周末能到場。
listening.promptZh: 熱情與實際安排有甚麼分別？

options.en: The goal motivated the group, but attendance still needed individual confirmation.
options.zh: 目標激起小組幹勁，但出席仍需要各自確認。

options.en: Everyone had already agreed to attend every weekend before the talk.
options.zh: 談話之前，每人都已同意每個周末出席。

options.en: The organiser regarded wanting to help as sufficient confirmation of attendance.
options.zh: 統籌人把想幫忙，當成已足夠確認出席。

options.en: The group lost interest because the goal gave no practical reason to help.
options.zh: 目標沒有提供實際幫忙理由，所以小組失去興趣。

listening.explanationZh: 清楚可做的改變帶來熱情，周末能否出席則仍須核對，不能互相代替。

reply.promptEn: What made the project feel worth helping with?
reply.promptZh: 甚麼讓大家覺得值得參與項目？

options.en: The clear goal fired us up by showing how our mapping could improve the path.
options.zh: 清楚目標說明地圖工作怎樣改善小徑，激起我們的幹勁。

options.en: We could see a practical use for the difficult sections we would record.
options.zh: 我們能看見，記下難走路段有實際用途。

options.en: The proposal connected our work with making the route easier for people to use.
options.zh: 建議把我們的工作，與讓人更易使用路線連起來。

options.en: A specific improvement gave us a reason to want to contribute.
options.zh: 一項具體改善，給我們想貢獻的理由。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出清楚的實際作用如何帶來動機，不宣稱已排定人手。

options.en: The goal fired us up, but we should ask who can attend on Saturday before treating the enthusiasm as a confirmed rota.

options.en: I thought wanting to help meant every person had already checked Saturday against their other plans.

options.en: I assumed the successful first trial meant we could assign the practical tasks without asking what each person had done before.
options.zh: 我以為首次試驗成功，就表示不用問每人過往做過甚麼，也可分派實務任務。

dialogue.explanationZh: 幹勁不等於已確認出席；一次小組試驗成功，也不能代替了解每人的實務經驗。時間與分工都仍需具體確認。

speaking.en: The first successful trial fired the group up, but they still needed to agree what they could realistically do next.

examples.en: A short scene we each care about could fire us up more than another page of copied notes. Could everyone choose a passage to read aloud, then tell us which question about the drama they want to explore?

examples.en: Let us try to fire up the group by hearing a few scenes people have chosen, rather than assume more copying will restore our interest. After the readings, I would like to ask what you want to investigate next.
examples.zh: 我們試着聽幾段大家自己選的場景，重新激起小組熱情，不假定多抄筆記就能恢復興趣。讀完後，我想問大家下一步想研究甚麼。

lessons.titleEn: the energy we carry often speaks before we do

target.pattern: \bthe energy we carry (?:often )?speaks before we do\b

brief.meaningEn: Our visible manner or emotional tone can communicate something before we begin speaking.
brief.meaningZh: 我們可見的表現或情緒基調，可能在開口前已向別人傳達某種感覺。
brief.grammar: The energy we carry often speaks before we do is a creative personification. We needs a clear group reference; often is a tendency, not a guarantee that observers interpret us correctly.
brief.register: Contextual energy-as-communicator metaphor, not a separately fixed idiom or a claim about measurable physical energy. Impressions and actual intentions may differ.
brief.boundaryZh: 別人可能先從姿態、步伐或表情形成印象，但不能因此確定動機、人格或每次情緒。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把第一眼印象當成已確認，也不要求人假裝愉快；可以清楚交代自己的狀態及可提供的協助。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明可見表現與第一印象的關係，並以實際溝通核對理解。

sources.expression: the energy we carry often speaks before we do
sources.sentence: In tense meetings, the energy we carry often speaks before we do.

listening.en: At the welcome desk, the energy we carry often speaks before we do: I arrived rushing and frowning, and a visitor wondered whether I was annoyed. I explained that I had missed a bus and was ready to help her.
listening.zh: 在接待處，我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒：我匆忙皺眉到場，一位訪客以為我可能不高興。我解釋自己錯過了巴士，也已準備好幫她。
listening.promptZh: 第一印象與解釋有甚麼分別？

options.en: The visitor formed an impression from the arrival, and the speaker then explained its cause and offered help.
options.zh: 訪客從到場表現形成印象，說話者之後解釋原因並提供協助。

options.en: The visitor had heard a refusal to help before noticing the expression.
options.zh: 訪客先聽到拒絕協助，之後才留意表情。

options.en: The speaker confirmed that the visitor herself had caused the annoyance.
options.zh: 說話者確認，不高興是訪客本人造成的。

options.en: The account says nobody noticed the rushed arrival until after the full explanation.
options.zh: 敘述說，完整解釋之後才有人留意匆忙到場。

listening.explanationZh: 可見表現引發猜想，但實際原因仍需本人說明，不能直接等同對訪客的不滿。

reply.promptEn: Why did you explain the missed bus to the visitor?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼向訪客解釋錯過巴士？

options.en: The energy we carry often speaks before we do, and my rushed arrival had created an impression I wanted to clarify.
options.zh: 我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒，我匆忙到場已形成印象，所以想澄清。

options.en: I wanted to distinguish my travel frustration from my willingness to help her.
options.zh: 我想分清交通上的焦急與願意幫她的態度。

options.en: She had noticed my expression, so an explanation could give context she did not yet have.
options.zh: 她留意到表情，所以解釋可以提供她尚未知道的背景。

options.en: My first appearance did not tell her what had actually happened on the journey.
options.zh: 我到場時的樣子，沒有告訴她途中實際發生了甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出先形成的印象需要背景，不宣稱表情能準確說明全部原因。

scene.promptZh: 一位主持安靜地走進房間，大家還未交談；觀察者只因她表情嚴肅，就說已確定她不想接待任何人。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: The energy we carry can suggest an impression before we speak, but the observer still needs to ask what her expression means here.
options.zh: 表現可以在開口前帶出印象，但觀察者仍須了解，她的表情在這裏代表甚麼。

options.en: The serious expression records her explicit decision not to welcome anyone.
options.zh: 嚴肅表情記錄了她明確決定不接待任何人。

options.en: The account includes her explanation that the visitors are unwelcome.
options.zh: 敘述包括她已解釋，訪客不受歡迎。

scene.explanationZh: 先有印象不等於已知動機；目前沒有她本人交代態度的資料。

options.en: 可見表現可能影響第一印象。
每位觀察者都會準確理解對方內心。
仍可用談話澄清狀態及意思。

contrast.explanationZh: 圖像談印象形成，不保證理解準確或人人看法相同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「訪客看你皺眉，已知道你不喜歡她，不用解釋吧？」你其實因交通焦急。哪句最好？

options.en: The energy we carry often speaks before we do, but I can explain the missed bus rather than let an impression stand as my intention.
options.zh: 我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒，但我可以解釋錯過巴士，不讓印象代替自己的意思。

options.en: I thought her first impression already established what had caused my expression.
options.zh: 我以為她的第一印象，已足以確定我表情的成因。

options.en: I assumed my hurried arrival had already communicated that I wanted to help quickly, so I did not need to offer help in words.
options.zh: 我以為匆忙到場已傳達想快點幫忙的意思，所以不用開口提出協助。

dialogue.explanationZh: 我的表現可能造成第一印象，卻不保證訪客已知道交通原因或幫忙意願；親自說明才可澄清。

speaking.en: The energy we carry often speaks before we do, but a clear greeting can help others understand what we are ready to offer.
speaking.zh: 我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒，但清楚招呼可以幫別人理解我們準備提供甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把第一印象與可以澄清的招呼連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們將首次探訪一間社區工場，幾位隊員常一到場就急着拍照。你要寫隊內事前提醒，提議先收好相機、停一下跟主人打招呼，再問能否記錄，不要求每人假裝同一心情。用一至兩句英文提出實際到訪安排。

examples.en: The energy we carry often speaks before we do, so let us put the cameras away and greet our hosts before asking to record anything. A short pause will give us room to explain the visit and hear what they are comfortable sharing.
examples.zh: 我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒，所以問能否記錄之前，先收好相機，向主人打招呼吧。短暫停一下，可以讓我們解釋到訪目的，也聽主人願意分享甚麼。

examples.en: Since the energy we carry often speaks before we do, I suggest arriving with the cameras packed rather than already taking photographs. We can begin with a greeting, explain our purpose and ask what recording, if any, the hosts would welcome.
examples.zh: 既然表現往往在開口前已傳出情緒，我建議到場時先把相機收好，不要已在拍照。我們可以先打招呼、解釋目的，再問主人是否歡迎記錄，以及願意接受哪種。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出到場時可實行的行動次序：先收相機及招呼，再解釋和詢問，不用假裝心情，也不把到場等同已有拍攝許可。

takeaways.en: The energy we carry often speaks before we do; the team decided to slow down at the entrance and introduce the visit properly.
takeaways.zh: 我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒；團隊決定在入口放慢腳步，好好介紹到訪目的。

takeaways.en: At the meeting, the energy we carry often speaks before we do: his folded arms seemed distant until he explained that he was cold.
takeaways.zh: 會上，我們的表現往往未開口就傳出情緒：他交叉雙臂的樣子顯得疏離，直到他解釋自己覺得冷。

options.en: The hours put in cover measuring, stitching and clearing, with twenty hours recorded altogether.

scene.explanationZh: 比較前要知道計了哪些活動，不能只靠相同數字建立相同範圍。

contrast.explanationZh: 時間記錄與技巧或成品質素評估不同，不能自行增加量度項目。

options.en: The hours put in show recorded time, but we need different evidence before judging skill or quality.
options.zh: 投入時數顯示已記錄的時間，但判斷技巧或質素之前，需要不同證據。

options.en: I thought a longer recorded duration was enough to identify the most skilful person.

options.en: I would compare the totals before asking whether preparation and clearing were counted in the same way.

dialogue.explanationZh: 先保留時間資料的用途，再分開了解技巧及記錄範圍，不用一個指標代替全部判斷。

speaking.en: Before comparing the hours put in, we should agree whether the record includes preparation and clearing afterwards.
speaking.zh: 比較投入時數前，應先議定記錄是否包括準備及事後收拾。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再明確詢問時間記錄的範圍。

examples.en: Before we plan next term, could you estimate the hours put in arranging the interviews and preparing the transcripts, as well as the recording time? A thirty-minute recording does not tell us how much preparation and follow-up the schedule needs to allow.
examples.zh: 安排下學期前，除了錄音時間，你們可否估計聯絡受訪者及整理逐字稿投入的時數？三十分鐘錄音，不能說明日程應預留多少準備及後續時間。

examples.en: The hours put in are not fully described by the length of each recording, so I need your estimates for arranging visits and editing transcripts. Could you send those separately before we agree next term’s timetable?
examples.zh: 每次錄音長度不足以完整描述投入時數，所以我需要你們估計安排探訪及編輯逐字稿的時間。議定下學期時間表前，可否把兩部分分開傳來？

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫實際補資料的請求，指定聯絡與逐字稿兩部分及編排日程的用途；不把錄音長度或回應者估算說成已完成的全部工時。

takeaways.en: The coordinator recorded the hours put in before opening day as well as the time spent welcoming visitors.

brief.meaningEn: Cause substantial mental tiredness through demanding or repeated thinking, using wear out as a figurative result.
brief.meaningZh: 以wear out的耗損意象，描述費神或反覆思考令人心力疲憊。
brief.grammar: Constant decisions can wear out the mind; wore/worn out. This causative mind-object frame makes the mental effort explicit. It is not a clinical label or a claim about permanent loss of ability.
brief.register: Contextual cognitive use of wear out, related to wear yourself out but with a named mental-effort object. Prefer concrete reported effects over a universal claim about everyone’s mind.
brief.boundaryZh: 疲憊不等於能力或興趣永久消失，也不能從一次難題推斷臨床狀況；要交代當事人實際感受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需要思考不表示一定心力耗盡；同樣，暫時休息不等於拒絕整項任務。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述心力負擔，並提出有範圍的工作調整而不自作診斷。
