sources.sentence: Constant decisions can wear out the mind.

listening.en: Checking every tiny layout choice seemed to wear out my mind by the end of the afternoon. I found myself rereading the same paragraph without deciding, so I saved the remaining choices for a fresh look the next morning.
listening.zh: 到下午結束時，反覆核對每個細微版面選擇，彷彿耗盡了我的心力。我發現自己重讀同一段卻不能決定，所以把其餘選擇留到翌晨精神較好時再看。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼反應支持疲憊？說話者怎樣處理？

options.en: Repeated rereading without deciding led the speaker to save the remaining choices for the next morning.
options.zh: 重讀仍不能決定，讓說話者把其餘選擇留待翌晨。

options.en: The speaker completed all the choices without needing to revisit any paragraph.
options.zh: 說話者完成全部選擇，不用重看任何段落。

options.en: The account gives a permanent diagnosis about the speaker’s ability to read.
options.zh: 敘述給出說話者閱讀能力的永久診斷。

options.en: The speaker abandoned the whole publication rather than return to the choices later.
options.zh: 說話者放棄整本刊物，不再回頭處理選擇。

listening.explanationZh: 這是本人描述的反覆思考及暫時疲憊，後續仍有再看的安排，不是永久能力判斷。

reply.promptEn: Why did you leave the remaining choices until morning?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把其餘選擇留待早上？

options.en: The repeated decisions seemed to wear out my mind, and rereading was no longer helping me choose.
options.zh: 反覆決定看來耗盡心力，重讀已無助我選擇。

options.en: I was mentally tired enough to revisit the same passage without reaching a decision.
options.zh: 我已心力疲憊，反覆看同一段也作不出決定。

options.en: A fresh look seemed more useful than continuing the unproductive rereading.
options.zh: 精神較好時再看，似乎比繼續無效重讀有用。

options.en: I was making no progress while tired, so I wanted to return after a pause rather than abandon the task.
options.zh: 疲累時我沒有進展，所以想暫停後回來處理，而不是放棄任務。

reply.explanationZh: 四句各自解釋暫停與繼續處理的安排，不把疲憊擴成永久不能做。

scene.promptZh: 學員第一次看一個難題，說自己有興趣，也有精神，想再試不同方法；評論只因題目複雜，就說已把他心力耗盡。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: A complex question can require effort without establishing that it has worn out the mind of this learner.
options.zh: 複雜問題可以需要付出心力，但不表示已令這位學員心力耗盡。

options.en: The account reports that he can no longer concentrate and wants to stop.
options.zh: 敘述表示，他已無法集中，也想停下來。

options.en: The account describes him spending many hours on repeated attempts before losing concentration.
options.zh: 敘述說，他反覆嘗試了很多小時後，失去了集中力。

scene.explanationZh: 題目難度與當事人的實際疲憊不同，資料反而交代了精力及繼續嘗試的意願。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「The task seemed to wear out my mind」推論？

options.en: 說話者把任務描述為令人心力疲憊。
說話者已永久失去理解這類工作的能力。
可以再問哪些反覆思考造成負擔。

contrast.explanationZh: 情境化疲憊描述不是永久能力或健康診斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你想明早再看，就表示再也不想做刊物吧？」你仍打算完成選擇。哪句最好？

options.en: The repeated choices seemed to wear out my mind today, but a pause is part of finishing the task, not a decision to leave it.
options.zh: 今天反覆選擇看來耗盡心力，但暫停是為了完成任務，不是決定放棄。

options.en: I thought needing a break meant I had already lost all interest in the publication.
options.zh: 我以為需要休息，就表示已對刊物完全失去興趣。

options.en: I assumed returning to the choices tomorrow meant postponing the publication deadline as well, rather than just pausing this evening’s review.
options.zh: 我以為明天再看選擇，就表示刊物期限也要順延，不只是今晚暫停覆核。

dialogue.explanationZh: 說話者仍打算完成刊物，只把尚未決定的部分留待翌晨；這不自行表示失去興趣或順延整份刊物的期限。

speaking.en: Repeated small decisions can wear out the mind, so I want to record the open questions before returning to them tomorrow.
speaking.zh: 反覆的小決定可能耗盡心力，所以我想先記下未解問題，明天再回來處理。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再交代暫停前如何保留未完成的工作。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫一部小說的短評。Lia一整天在家事和工作之間反覆作小決定，晚上重讀同一封信也選不出怎樣回覆；下一章卻寫她清楚解決一個新問題。用一至兩句英文分析這一晚的疲憊與人物長期能力的分別，不把一幕當成永久無能或健康診斷。

examples.en: Here, repeated choices appear to wear out the mind, as Lia rereads the same letter without choosing a reply. The next chapter shows her solving a new problem, so this scene presents temporary fatigue rather than her whole ability.
examples.zh: 這裏，反覆選擇彷彿耗盡心力，Lia重讀同一封信也選不出怎樣回覆。下一章卻寫她解決新問題，所以這一幕呈現暫時疲憊，而不是她全部的能力。

examples.en: The novel shows how everyday decisions can wear out the mind for an evening without defining the character’s lasting ability. Lia’s clearer response to a new problem in the following chapter changes how we should read the earlier hesitation.
examples.zh: 小說展示，日常決定可以讓人一晚心力耗盡，卻不能據此界定角色長期的能力。下一章Lia更清楚地回應新問題，改變了我們應怎樣理解較早的猶豫。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫實際小說短評，把重讀及無法決定連到當晚疲憊，也用下一章表現限制推論，不自作健康診斷或永久能力判斷。

takeaways.en: She felt that the constant comparisons could wear out the mind, so she asked which decisions truly needed attention that day.
takeaways.zh: 她覺得不斷比較可能耗盡心力，便問哪些決定當天真的需要處理。

takeaways.en: After hours of reviewing tiny changes, she felt that another round could wear out her mind without improving the draft.
takeaways.zh: 看了數小時的細微改動後，她覺得再來一輪可能耗盡心力，卻不能改善初稿。

lessons.titleZh: 因長期使用而磨損失效

brief.meaningEn: Become damaged or no longer usable through use over time, or cause that deterioration.
brief.meaningZh: 物品因一段時間的使用而磨損，變得不好用或失效，也可指使用造成這種耗損。
brief.grammar: a strap wears out; wore out; has worn out; is wearing out. Transitive wear something out is also possible. Describe the affected component rather than assume an entire item is beyond repair.
brief.register: Common physical deterioration phrasal verb; distinguish a person being worn out with tiredness. Actual condition matters more than age alone.
brief.boundaryZh: 一個部件磨損不一定代表整件物品都要丟棄，使用年期也不能單獨確定狀況；要看具體損耗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 新物品暫時不運作，也未必是磨損，可能是設定或裝配問題；應分清原因。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述物品損耗及仍可使用的部分，提出有範圍的查問。

listening.en: The bag’s shoulder strap wore out after years of daily use: the stitching frayed until it could no longer hold the load. The zip and main compartment still worked, so I asked about replacing the strap rather than the whole bag.
listening.zh: 多年每天使用後，袋的肩帶磨損了：縫線逐漸鬆散，已不能承重。拉鏈及主袋仍可用，所以我詢問能否換肩帶，而不是換整個袋。
listening.promptZh: 損耗發生在哪裏？甚麼仍可用？

options.en: The strap’s stitching failed, while the zip and main compartment remained usable.
options.zh: 肩帶縫線失效，拉鏈及主袋仍可使用。

options.en: The zip failed first, leaving a new shoulder strap as the only usable part.
options.zh: 拉鏈先失效，只剩新肩帶可用。

options.en: The bag had never been used, and the issue was only a loose packing clip.
options.zh: 袋從未使用，問題只是一個鬆開的包裝夾。

options.en: The speaker had already discarded the whole bag without asking about its strap.
options.zh: 說話者未詢問肩帶，就已丟棄整個袋。

listening.explanationZh: 具體損耗在肩帶縫線，不能把一個部件的失效擴成所有部分都壞了。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask about replacing just the strap?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼只問換肩帶？

options.en: The strap had worn out, but the other main parts of the bag were still usable.
options.zh: 肩帶已磨損失效，但袋的其他主要部分仍可用。

options.en: The damage was in the stitching that held the load, not the zip or main compartment.
options.zh: 損壞在承重的縫線，不是拉鏈或主袋。

options.en: The other functions still worked, so I wanted to check a repair of the failed component before replacing the whole item.
options.zh: 其他功能仍正常，所以換整件物品前，我想先了解能否修理失效部件。

options.en: The bag’s remaining functions gave me a reason to ask about a smaller replacement.
options.zh: 袋仍有可用功能，所以我想問能否只換較小部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都依據損壞位置及其他功能，沒有先保證一定能修好。

scene.promptZh: 一盞剛拆包的枱燈不亮，後來發現開關仍在運送鎖定狀態，解除後便正常。有人只因開始不亮，就說已磨損。哪句較準確？

options.en: The initial failure did not show that the lamp had worn out; the account identifies a setup issue that was resolved.
options.zh: 起初不亮，不表示枱燈已磨損；敘述指出的是後來解決了的設定問題。

options.en: The account documents years of use before the lamp stopped working.
options.zh: 敘述記錄，枱燈使用多年後才停止運作。

options.en: Unlocking the switch is described as replacing a component damaged by prolonged use.
options.zh: 解除開關鎖定，被描述為更換因長期使用而損壞的部件。

scene.explanationZh: 不能把任何不運作都稱為磨損，這次已有具體設定原因。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只因「One component has worn out」便確定？

options.en: 有一個部件因使用而耗損。
整件物品已沒有任何可保留或修理的部分。
可以詢問是哪個部件及其狀況。

contrast.explanationZh: 部件與整件物品不同，仍需了解其餘部分及能否處理。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「肩帶壞，就直接說袋全部失效吧？」你知道拉鏈和主袋仍正常。哪句最好？

options.en: The strap wore out, but I should describe that component accurately and ask about replacement before judging the whole bag.
options.zh: 肩帶磨損了，但應準確描述那個部件，先問能否更換，再判斷整個袋。

options.en: I thought a failed strap established that the zip had also stopped working.
options.zh: 我以為肩帶失效，就足以確定拉鏈也不能用了。

options.en: I would judge every part from the bag’s age without checking which functions remain.
options.zh: 我會只按袋的年期判斷每個部分，不查哪些功能仍在。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按已知部件及功能說明，比從一項損壞或年期概括全部更準確。

speaking.en: The cover has worn out around the hinge, but I want to check whether the inside pages can be kept when it is repaired.
speaking.zh: 封面在接合處磨損了，但修理時我想先問內頁能否保留。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述損壞位置及想保留的部分。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為舊車票打孔器寫展牌。記錄說它長年使用，切口部件已磨鈍而不能正常打孔；資料沒有使用者姓名或確切年份。用一至兩句英文寫實際展牌文字，描述損耗及用途，不從磨損自行指定某位職員或日期。

examples.en: The cutting part has worn out through repeated use, leaving this ticket punch unable to make a clean hole. The wear tells us about its condition, but the surviving record does not identify an operator or an exact year.
examples.zh: 切口部件因反覆使用而磨損，令這個車票打孔器無法打出完整孔洞。磨損交代了它的狀況，但現存記錄沒有指出使用者或確切年份。

examples.en: This ticket punch wore out at its cutting edge after years of use. Its condition is visible, while the names of its operators and the exact dates of use remain unrecorded.
examples.zh: 這個車票打孔器使用多年後，在切口處磨損失效。它的狀況可見，但使用者姓名及確切使用日期仍未有記錄。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫可展示的器物說明，分清可見的損耗與仍無記錄的身份日期，不讓具體物件描述變成虛構歷史。

takeaways.en: The wheels wore out before the frame, so the owner asked whether new wheels would fit the old trolley.
takeaways.zh: 輪子比車架先磨損，物主便問新輪子能否裝在舊手推車上。

takeaways.en: A faded label does not by itself show that the whole device has worn out.
takeaways.zh: 標籤褪色，本身不表示整部裝置都已磨損失效。

lessons.titleEn: take someone or something for granted
lessons.titleZh: 把人或事物視為理所當然而少有珍惜

target.pattern: \b(?:take|takes|taking|took|taken)(?: (?:him|her|them|it|you|me|the volunteers|their help|the help|the map|today[’\']s comfort))? for granted\b

brief.meaningEn: Fail to appreciate a person, contribution or benefit because it is familiar or assumed to be available.
brief.meaningZh: 因人、貢獻或好處太熟悉，或以為隨時可得，而沒有好好重視及感謝。
brief.grammar: take someone/something for granted, including a familiar benefit such as today’s comfort; take for granted + a longer noun phrase; be taken for granted. Took/taken/taking. Distinguish appreciation from the separate assume-true sense in take it for granted that....
brief.register: Established idiom, often critical of unexamined expectations. A parent may remind a teenager not to take today’s comfort for granted while recognising the work behind it; gratitude does not assume future help.
brief.boundaryZh: 少有重視與作出錯誤事實推論不同；應按上下文分清「不珍惜」和「未經查證便假定」兩種用法。
brief.misconceptionZh: 既有幫忙不等於永久承諾；肯定具體貢獻，也可詢問今後的範圍，而不只說一次謝謝。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體承認被忽略的價值，並避免把感謝變成對未來的要求。

listening.en: We had taken the volunteers for granted, thanking performers but rarely mentioning those who cleared the room. Jo explained the work after the audience left; we changed the acknowledgements and asked about future cover.
listening.zh: 我們把義工視為理所當然，只感謝表演者，很少提及收拾房間的人。Jo解釋觀眾離開後的工作，我們才修改鳴謝，也詢問往後的人手安排。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼價值原先被忽略？後來怎樣回應？

options.en: The clearing work was overlooked, then acknowledged while future cover was discussed.
options.zh: 收拾工作原先被忽略，後來得到肯定，也有人討論往後的人手。

options.en: The volunteers had agreed to every future clearing shift before Jo spoke.
options.zh: Jo開口前，義工已同意往後每次收拾輪值。

options.en: The performers alone did all the clearing after the audience left.
options.zh: 觀眾離開後，全部收拾都只由表演者處理。

options.en: Jo asked for the clearing work to be removed from the acknowledgements.
options.zh: Jo要求在鳴謝中刪去收拾工作。

listening.explanationZh: 原先少被提及的是幕後收拾；之後既肯定貢獻，也另行詢問人手，而不是預先代義工承諾。

reply.promptEn: What did Jo’s explanation make you reconsider?
reply.promptZh: Jo的解釋讓你們重新考慮甚麼？

options.en: We had taken the volunteers for granted instead of recognising the work after the audience left.
options.zh: 我們把義工視為理所當然，沒有重視觀眾離開後的工作。

options.en: Our thanks had overlooked people who did essential clearing.
options.zh: 我們的致謝忽略了負責必要收拾的人。

options.en: The end of the performance was not the end of everyone’s work.
options.zh: 演出結束，不表示每人的工作都結束。

options.en: We needed to acknowledge the contribution and discuss cover, rather than assume it would continue.
options.zh: 我們需要肯定貢獻並討論人手，不假定幫忙會一直繼續。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明被忽略的工作與需要改變的期待，沒有用感謝替人答應下一次。

options.en: The sentence explicitly criticises the writer for not thanking the person who opens the room.
options.zh: 句子明確批評作者，沒有感謝負責開門的人。

options.en: The report says the writer checked the opening with the manager before making the assumption.
options.zh: 報告說作者先向經理核對開放安排，才作出假定。

那人已同意以後任何時間都提供相同協助。

lessons.titleZh: 不能只靠表格分析來運作

target.pattern: \brun(?:s|ning)? on spreadsheets alone\b|\bran on spreadsheets alone\b

brief.meaningEn: Function relying only on tabular planning or analysis; usually denied to emphasise practical work and human needs beyond the figures.
brief.meaningZh: 只依靠表格規劃或分析來運作；通常用否定句，強調數字以外的實際工作及人的需要。
brief.grammar: A city/centre cannot run on spreadsheets alone. Run means function; alone restricts the means of support. The negation does not say spreadsheets are useless.
brief.register: A productive operational metaphor, not a fixed idiom or a claim that every spreadsheet has inaccurate data. Explain which practical needs the figures cannot fulfil by themselves.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只靠表格，不等於完全不用資料；應指出還需要實際觀察、工作或溝通中的哪些部分。
brief.misconceptionZh: 完整的表格可能有幫助，但不會自己開門、準備器材或代替使用者說明經驗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把資料與實際工作連起來，提出具體補充而不把兩者對立。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A city cannot run on spreadsheets alone.

listening.en: The arts centre cannot run on spreadsheets alone. Its booking sheet showed free rooms, but a coordinator still had to confirm who could unlock them and whether the equipment was ready before accepting the school’s request.
listening.zh: 藝術中心不能只靠試算表運作。預訂表顯示有空房，但接受學校要求前，統籌人仍須確認誰能開門，以及器材是否準備好。
listening.promptZh: 表格有甚麼作用？甚麼仍需另外確認？

options.en: It showed room availability, while people still had to confirm access and equipment.
options.zh: 它顯示空房情況，但人仍須確認開門及器材。

options.en: A free-room entry already confirmed a person to unlock it and all equipment to use.
options.zh: 表格列出空房，已確認有人開門及所有器材可用。

options.en: The centre had decided to reject all booking information as useless.
options.zh: 中心已決定，全部預訂資料都沒有用。

options.en: The coordinator accepted the request before asking about access or equipment.
options.zh: 統籌人先接受要求，再問開門及器材。

listening.explanationZh: 房間資料有用，但不等於所有使用條件已準備好；還需要具體確認。

reply.promptEn: Why was the free-room entry not enough to accept the request?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼單靠空房記錄，還不足以接受要求？

options.en: The centre cannot run on spreadsheets alone; someone still needed to confirm access and equipment.
options.zh: 中心不能只靠試算表運作，仍要有人確認開門及器材。

options.en: An available room did not establish that the school could enter it and use what it needed.
options.zh: 房間有空，不代表學校已能進去並使用所需器材。

options.en: The record covered one part of the arrangement, leaving practical conditions to check.
options.zh: 記錄涵蓋安排的一部分，實際條件仍須核對。

options.en: People had to connect the room information with the actual opening and preparation work.
options.zh: 人需要把房間資料，與實際開門及準備工作連起來。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留表格資料的作用，同時指出它不能單獨完成使用安排。

scene.promptZh: 小組用表格整理園地尺寸，也實地查看排水及通道，再向使用者查問需要。評論只見表格，就說他們完全忽略現場。哪句較準確？

options.en: Using a spreadsheet does not mean the group expects the project to run on spreadsheets alone; the account includes site checks and conversations.
options.zh: 使用試算表，不表示小組打算只靠表格運作項目；敘述也有實地查看及談話。

options.en: The account describes a plan made entirely from the table without visiting the garden.
options.zh: 敘述描述，計劃全部來自表格，沒有到過園地。

options.en: The spreadsheet is said to replace the conversations with the people using the space.
options.zh: 敘述說，試算表取代了與使用者的談話。

scene.explanationZh: 資料工具與現場了解可以並用，不能只因見到表格，就否定已交代的實務。

contrast.promptZh: 「A city cannot run on spreadsheets alone」最不能直接表示哪項？

options.en: 城市運作還需要表格分析以外的工作。
表格資料在任何安排中都沒有用途。
可以舉實際工作或人的需要來說明限制。

contrast.explanationZh: alone及cannot否定只靠一種方式，不是把資料工具全部否定。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「不能只靠表格，就不用記房間了吧？」你仍需要知道哪天有空。哪句最好？

options.en: We cannot run on spreadsheets alone, but the booking data still helps when we combine it with people checking access and equipment.
options.zh: 我們不能只靠試算表運作，但把預訂資料與人工核對開門及器材連起來，仍有幫助。

options.en: I thought questioning reliance on the sheet meant the room dates no longer mattered.
options.zh: 我以為質疑只靠表格，就表示房間日期不再重要。

options.en: I would inspect the equipment without checking whether the room had already been booked.
options.zh: 我會只看器材，不查房間是否已被預訂。

dialogue.explanationZh: 一方面不能只靠表格，另一方面也不能忽略有用日期；需要把兩種資料接合。

speaking.en: The service cannot run on spreadsheets alone, but clear records can help the people doing the practical work coordinate their next steps.
speaking.zh: 服務不能只靠試算表運作，但清楚記錄可以幫實際工作的人協調下一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把記錄工具與人的工作連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替校刊訪問社區修補活動的統籌人。統計只有修好物品的數目，還看不出接待、了解損壞及教使用者的工作。用一至兩句英文寫實際訪問問題，請對方帶你看一件物品由到場至交還的過程，不先斷言數據無用。

examples.en: The service cannot run on spreadsheets alone, so could you walk us through one item from arrival to return? I would like to understand the reception, questions and teaching behind the repair total, rather than treat the number as the whole process.
examples.zh: 服務不能只靠試算表運作，所以你可否帶我們看一件物品由到場至交還的過程？我想了解修好物品總數背後的接待、查問及教學，不把數字當成全部流程。

examples.en: Could you show how the activity works beyond its count of completed repairs, since it cannot run on spreadsheets alone? Please take one example through the conversations with its owner and the explanation given before it is returned.
examples.zh: 活動不能只靠試算表運作，你可否說明修好物品數目以外，它實際怎樣進行？請用一個例子，帶我們看與物主的談話，以及交還前的解釋。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫具體訪問問題，以一件物品的流程了解數字背後的工作，不預先指責統籌人，也不把計數說成完全沒有用。

takeaways.en: The library cannot run on spreadsheets alone; its records support staff who still need to understand what readers are asking for.
takeaways.zh: 圖書館不能只靠試算表運作，記錄支持職員，但職員仍要理解讀者的需要。

takeaways.en: Their review asks which parts of the service can be planned from data and why it cannot run on spreadsheets alone.
takeaways.zh: 檢討詢問服務哪些部分可用資料規劃，以及為甚麼不能只靠試算表運作。
